48285.e: It is cold all year round around Antarctica. The water is often only just above freezing point.
48285.m: The water in the Southern Ocean is ice cold.

48286.q: Which fish in the icy Southern Ocean have a kind of antifreeze in their blood?
48286.e: Icefish live in the sea around Antarctica. Special substances in their bodies stop them from freezing in the icy water.
48286.m: Icefish have a kind of antifreeze in their blood.

48287.q: Which seabird with huge wings glides over the Southern Ocean?
48287.e: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of all birds, about 3 metres. It can glide over the sea for hours without flapping its wings.
48287.m: The albatross glides over the Southern Ocean.

48288.q: Which sea in Europe contains only a little salt?
48288.e: Many rivers with fresh water flow into the Baltic Sea. That is why it is much less salty than other seas.
48288.m: The Baltic Sea is only slightly salty.

48289.q: Roughly how much salt is in one litre of sea water?
48289.e: Sea water contains about 3.5 per cent salt on average. That is about 35 grams in one litre, or roughly seven teaspoons.
48289.m: One litre of sea water contains about 35 grams of salt.

48290.q: What is left behind when sea water evaporates in the sun?
48290.e: When it evaporates, only the water goes into the air. The salt stays behind.
48290.m: When sea water evaporates, salt is left behind.

48291.q: What is a place where salt is obtained from sea water called?
48291.e: At a saltworks, sea water is left to evaporate in shallow pools. Then the salt can be collected.
48291.m: Salt is obtained at a saltworks.

48292.q: Where does the salt in the sea come from?
48292.e: Rain dissolves tiny amounts of salt out of rocks. Rivers carry it into the sea, where it stays for a very long time.
48292.m: Rivers carry salt from rocks into the sea.

48293.q: Roughly how much of the Earth's surface is covered by sea?
48293.e: About 71 per cent of the Earth's surface is sea. That is why the Earth is also called the blue planet.
48293.m: Most of the Earth is covered by sea.

48294.q: What do we call water from lakes and rivers that is hardly salty?
48294.e: The water in Swiss lakes such as Lake Zurich or Lake Geneva is fresh water. It contains only very little salt.
48294.m: Lakes in Switzerland have fresh water.

48295.q: At roughly what temperature does sea water freeze?
48295.e: Salt in the water means it only freezes at a lower temperature. Sea water freezes at about minus 2 degrees Celsius.
48295.m: Sea water only freezes below zero degrees.

48296.q: Roughly how much of the water on Earth is salt water?
48296.e: Almost all the water on Earth is salty sea water. Only about 3 per cent is fresh water.
48296.m: Almost all the Earth's water is salty.

48297.q: What can you look up in a tide table?
a: when low tide and high tide are
when there is a full moon
48297.e: A tide table shows the times of high water and low water for each day. This is important for fishermen and walkers.
48297.m: A tide table shows the times of low and high tide.

48298.q: What is it called when the water at the seaside rises again?
48298.e: At high tide the water level rises. The water comes closer to the coast again.
48298.m: At high tide the water rises.

48299.e: The moon pulls on the Earth's water with its gravity. This makes the sea rise and fall.
48299.m: The moon pulls on the water of the seas.

48300.q: Roughly how often a day does high tide come on most coasts?
48300.e: On most coasts there are two high tides and two low tides every day.
48300.m: High tide usually comes twice a day.

48301.q: Roughly how much time passes from low tide to high tide?
48301.e: It takes a good 6 hours from low water to high water. Then the water goes down again.
48301.m: There are about 6 hours between low tide and high tide.

48302.q: What is the area on the North Sea that dries out at low tide called?
48302.e: In the Wadden Sea the seabed is exposed at low tide. Lots of worms, mussels and crabs live in it.
48302.m: The Wadden Sea dries out at low tide.

48303.q: What do we call low tide and high tide together?
48303.e: The regular rising and falling of the sea is called the tides.
48303.m: Low tide and high tide together are called the tides.

48304.q: Why are there hardly any tides in Swiss lakes?
a: The lakes are too high up
48304.e: Tides can only be clearly noticed in huge bodies of water such as the oceans. In a lake the difference is tiny.
48304.m: Lakes are too small for tides.

48305.q: What can you do with a guide in the Wadden Sea at low tide?
48305.e: At low tide you can walk on the seabed. Because the water comes back, it is best to go with an experienced guide.
48305.m: At low tide you can walk across the mudflats.

48306.q: What makes most of the waves on the sea?
48306.e: When wind blows over the water, waves form. The stronger and longer the wind blows, the higher they get.
48306.m: The wind makes the waves on the sea.

48307.q: What is the sport where you ride waves on a board called?
48307.e: When surfing you stand on a board and let a wave carry you.
48307.m: When surfing you ride the waves.

48308.q: What is the highest point of a wave called?
48308.e: The crest is the top part of a wave. It is often covered in white foam.
48308.m: The crest is at the top of the wave.

48309.q: What should you wear on a boat when the waves are high?
48309.e: A life jacket keeps your head above water if you fall into the sea. On boats it is especially important when the waves are high.
48309.m: A life jacket protects you on a boat.

48310.q: What is it called when waves tumble over at the coast?
48310.e: When a wave reaches shallow water, it breaks and tumbles over. This is called surf.
48310.m: At the coast the waves break in the surf.

48311.q: What is sand on the beach usually made of?
48311.e: Waves rub stones against each other for a very long time. This makes tiny grains, mostly of the mineral quartz.
48311.m: Sand is made of tiny grains of stone.

48312.q: What do you often find on the beach that comes from sea creatures?
48312.e: Mussels and sea snails live in the sea. Their empty shells are washed up on the beach by the waves.
48312.m: You often find seashells on the beach.

48313.q: What is a beach made of round stones instead of sand called?
48313.e: On a pebble beach there are lots of round stones. They were ground smooth and round by the waves.
48313.m: A pebble beach has stones instead of sand.

48314.q: What do you protect yourself from on the beach with sun cream and a sun hat?
48314.e: On the beach the sun is especially strong, because water and sand reflect the light. Sun cream and a hat protect your skin.
48314.m: On the beach you protect yourself from sunburn.

48315.q: Which ocean does the Caribbean Sea belong to?
48315.e: The Caribbean Sea is a side sea of the Atlantic. It lies between Central America and many islands.
48315.m: The Caribbean Sea is part of the Atlantic.

48316.q: Which is the largest island in the Caribbean?
48316.e: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean. Its capital is Havana. The second largest island is Hispaniola, with Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
48316.m: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

48317.q: Which island in the Caribbean is the home of reggae music?
48317.e: Reggae music began in Jamaica. Bob Marley is its best-known musician.

48318.q: What are the large and small groups of islands in the Caribbean called?
48318.e: The Caribbean islands are called the Greater and Lesser Antilles. Puerto Rico, for example, belongs to the Greater Antilles.
48318.m: The Caribbean islands are called the Antilles.

48319.q: Which explorer reached islands in the Caribbean in 1492?
48319.e: Christopher Columbus wanted to sail to India. But he came to islands in the Caribbean.

48320.q: In which country is the seaside resort of Cancún on the Caribbean Sea?
48320.e: Cancún is on the Yucatán Peninsula in the east of Mexico. Its beaches are on the warm Caribbean Sea.
48320.m: Cancún in Mexico is on the Caribbean Sea.

48321.q: What is the water in the Caribbean Sea usually like?
48321.e: The Caribbean is near the equator, in the tropics. So the water is pleasantly warm all year round.
48321.m: The sea in the Caribbean is warm.

48322.q: Which powerful storms happen in the Caribbean, especially in late summer?
48322.e: Huge rotating storms can form over the warm sea. In the Caribbean they are called hurricanes.
48322.m: There are hurricanes in the Caribbean.

48323.q: Which continent lies south of the Caribbean Sea?
48323.e: To the south of the Caribbean are countries such as Colombia and Venezuela. They belong to South America.
48323.m: South America lies south of the Caribbean.

48324.q: Between which two continents is the Red Sea?
48324.e: On the west side of the Red Sea is Africa, on the east side the Arabian Peninsula in Asia.
48324.m: The Red Sea separates Africa and Asia.

48325.q: Which country in Africa is on the Red Sea and is a popular holiday destination?
48325.e: Egypt has a long coast on the Red Sea. Places such as Hurghada are popular for beach holidays.
48325.m: Egypt is on the Red Sea.

48326.q: Which peninsula with a famous mountain lies at the north of the Red Sea?
48326.e: The Sinai Peninsula belongs to Egypt and lies between two arms of the Red Sea. Mount Sinai is there.
48326.m: The Sinai Peninsula is on the Red Sea.

48327.q: What is the Red Sea known for among divers?
48327.e: Lots of corals grow in the warm water of the Red Sea. Countless colourful fish live there.
48327.m: The Red Sea has beautiful coral reefs.

48328.q: Which large country on the Arabian Peninsula is on the Red Sea?
48328.e: Saudi Arabia has a long coast on the east shore of the Red Sea.
48328.m: Saudi Arabia is on the Red Sea.

48329.q: What is one explanation for the name ‘Red Sea’?
48329.e: Sometimes lots of algae grow in the water and turn the sea reddish. But there are other explanations for the name too.
48329.m: Reddish algae can colour the Red Sea.

48330.q: What is the water in the Red Sea like?
a: ice cold and with no salt
48330.e: It is hot by the Red Sea and it hardly rains. A lot of water evaporates, so it is saltier than most seas.
48330.m: The Red Sea is warm and very salty.

48331.q: Which ocean is the Red Sea connected to in the south?
48331.e: In the south a narrow strait leads to the Gulf of Aden. This belongs to the Indian Ocean.
48331.m: The Red Sea is part of the Indian Ocean.

48332.q: Which orange and white striped fish live in sea anemones in the Red Sea?
48332.e: Anemonefish, also called clownfish, live between the arms of sea anemones. There they are protected from enemies.

48333.q: Why is the Dead Sea called that?
a: Almost no creatures can live in it.
48333.e: The water is so salty that no fish can live in it. Only tiny living things such as bacteria survive.
48333.m: No fish can live in the Dead Sea.

48334.q: What is the Dead Sea really?
48334.e: The Dead Sea is not connected to an ocean. It is a lake with very salty water.
48334.m: The Dead Sea is really a salt lake.

48335.q: Which river flows into the Dead Sea?
48335.e: The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea from the north. The Dead Sea has no outflow.
48335.m: The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea.

48336.q: What is special about the shore of the Dead Sea?
a: It is the lowest place on land.
It is the highest place in the world.
It is the coldest place in the world.
It is the wettest place in the world.
48336.e: The shore is over 400 metres below sea level. No other place on land is so low.
48336.m: The Dead Sea is at the lowest place on land.

48337.q: Roughly how much saltier than an ocean is the Dead Sea?
48337.e: The Dead Sea has about eight to ten times as much salt dissolved in it as ocean water. That is why it is so salty that hardly anything lives in it.
48337.m: The Dead Sea is about ten times saltier than an ocean.

48338.q: What happens if you lie down in the water of the Dead Sea?
a: You have to paddle hard to stay up
48338.e: The very salty water is heavier than normal water. It holds up your body so well that you float like a cork.
48338.m: In the Dead Sea you float on top like a cork.

48339.q: Which country borders the Dead Sea to the east?
48339.e: Jordan is on the east shore of the Dead Sea. On the other side are Israel and the West Bank.
48339.m: Jordan is on the east shore of the Dead Sea.

48340.q: What forms on the shore of the Dead Sea when water evaporates?
48340.e: When the water evaporates in the heat, the salt is left behind. This makes white crusts and lumps of salt on the shore.
48340.m: Salt crusts form at the Dead Sea.

48341.q: What has been happening to the water level of the Dead Sea for many years?
48341.e: A lot of water is taken from the rivers for fields and cities. So the water level falls by about one metre every year.
48341.m: The Dead Sea gets smaller every year.

48342.q: On which continent are the Himalayas?
48342.e: The Himalayas are in Asia. They stretch across Nepal, India, Bhutan and China, among others.
48342.m: The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia.

48343.q: Which small country with a dragon on its flag is in the Himalayas?
48343.e: Bhutan is in the east of the Himalayas. Its flag shows a white dragon.
48343.m: Bhutan is a small country in the Himalayas.

48344.q: Which country lies right in the middle of the Himalayas?
48344.e: Nepal is a small country right in the middle of the Himalayas. Many of the highest mountains in the world are there.
48344.m: Nepal lies in the middle of the Himalayas.

48345.q: What is special about the Himalayas?
48345.e: The highest mountains on Earth are in the Himalayas. Many peaks are over 8000 metres high.
48345.m: The Himalayas have the highest mountains in the world.

48346.q: Which big cat lives in the mountains of the Himalayas?
48346.e: The snow leopard lives high up in the mountains of Asia. Its thick fur protects it from the cold.
48346.m: The snow leopard lives in the cold high mountains of Asia.

48347.q: Which animal with long, shaggy fur do people in the Himalayas use to carry loads?
48347.e: The yak is a type of cattle with long, thick fur. It can stand great cold and carries heavy loads.
48347.m: The yak is a shaggy type of cattle from the Himalayas.

48348.q: Which reddish brown animal with a bushy tail lives in the mountain forests of the Himalayas?
48348.e: The red panda is about the size of a cat. It lives in bamboo forests in the Himalayas and eats mainly bamboo.
48348.m: The red panda lives in the forests of the Himalayas.

48349.q: What are mountains higher than 8000 metres called?
48349.e: Mountains over 8000 metres are called eight-thousanders. There are only 14 of them in the world, all in Asia.
48349.m: There are only 14 eight-thousanders on Earth.

48350.q: What is the legendary creature said to live in the Himalayas called?
48350.e: The yeti is a creature from legends and stories. Nobody has ever found one.
48350.m: The yeti is a legendary creature from the Himalayas.

48351.q: What often flutters in the wind on the summit of Mount Everest?
48351.e: Climbers often hang colourful prayer flags at the top. These flags are part of the faith of many people in the Himalayas.
48351.m: Colourful prayer flags flutter on Everest.

48352.q: In which month do most climbers reach the summit of Mount Everest?
48352.e: In May the wind on the summit is usually weaker. After that the rainy season begins, with lots of snow in the mountains.
48352.m: Most climbers stand on Everest in May.

48353.q: What do we call many mountains that together form a long chain?
48353.e: A mountain range is made up of many mountains, valleys and passes. The Alps, for example, are a mountain range.
48353.m: Many mountains together form a mountain range.

48354.q: In which year did people first stand on top of Mount Everest?
48354.e: On 29 May 1953 two climbers from a British expedition reached the summit. They were the first people up there.
48354.m: Mount Everest was first climbed in 1953.

48355.q: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world. What is the second highest called?
48355.e: K2 is 8611 metres high and is in the Karakoram range in Asia. It is thought to be even harder to climb than Mount Everest.
48355.m: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

48356.q: Who is Mount Everest named after?
48356.e: The mountain was named after George Everest. He used to be in charge of surveying the land in India.
48356.m: Mount Everest bears the name of the surveyor George Everest.

48357.q: What do people in Nepal call Mount Everest?
48357.e: In Nepal the mountain is called Sagarmatha. In Tibet it is called Chomolungma.
48357.m: In Nepal Mount Everest is called Sagarmatha.

48358.q: Why is breathing so hard on Mount Everest?
48358.e: The higher you climb, the thinner the air becomes. On the summit you get much less oxygen with every breath.
48358.m: On high mountains the air is thin.

48359.q: Which mountain range does Mount Everest belong to?
48359.e: Mount Everest is the highest peak in the Himalayas. This mountain range is in Asia.
48359.m: Mount Everest belongs to the Himalayas.

48360.q: Which small rodent with very soft fur comes from the Andes?
48360.e: The chinchilla lives in the wild high up in the Andes. Its thick fur is one of the softest of all animals.
48360.m: The chinchilla comes from the Andes.

48361.q: What is special about the Andes?
48361.e: The Andes are about 7000 kilometres long. No other mountain range on land is as long.
48361.m: The Andes are the longest mountain range on land.

48362.q: Which long, narrow country lies on the west side of the Andes?
48362.e: Chile is very long and narrow. To the east are the Andes, to the west the Pacific.
48362.m: Chile lies between the Andes and the Pacific.

48363.q: Which bird with pink feathers lives by salt lakes high in the Andes?
48363.e: In the Andes there are salt lakes high up. There flamingos eat tiny algae and shrimps from the water.
48363.m: Flamingos also live by salt lakes in the Andes.

48364.q: Which huge bird glides high above the mountains of South America?
48364.e: The Andean condor is one of the largest birds that can fly. It glides far over the mountains of the Andes.
48364.m: The condor glides over the Andes.

48365.q: Which capital city in South America lies high in the Andes?
48365.e: Quito is the capital of Ecuador. It lies at a height of about 2800 metres in the Andes.
48365.m: Quito lies high in the Andes.

48366.q: Which people once had a great empire in the Andes?
48366.e: The Inca lived in the Andes. Their empire was very large about 500 years ago. The Aztecs, Maya and Olmecs lived further north, in Central America.
48366.m: The Inca had a great empire in the Andes.

48367.q: Which fire-spitting mountains are there lots of in the Andes?
48367.e: There are very many volcanoes in the Andes. Some of them still erupt today.
48367.m: There are many volcanoes in the Andes.

48368.q: Which animal with a long neck and soft wool carries loads in the Andes?
48368.e: Llamas live high in the Andes. People there use them to carry loads and make warm clothes from their wool.
48368.m: The llama lives in the Andes.

48369.q: On which continent are the Rocky Mountains?
48369.e: The Rocky Mountains are in the west of North America. They stretch across Canada and the USA.
48369.m: The Rocky Mountains are in North America.

48370.q: Which animal builds dams of wood in the streams of the Rocky Mountains?
48370.e: The beaver cuts down trees with its sharp teeth. It builds dams and a lodge in the water out of branches and mud.
48370.m: The beaver builds dams in streams.

48371.q: What are the Rocky Mountains often called for short?
48371.e: Many people simply say ‘Rockies’. That is shorter and easier to say.
48371.m: The Rocky Mountains are called the Rockies for short.

48373.q: Which big bear lives in the Rocky Mountains?
48373.e: The grizzly is a large brown bear. It lives in the forests and mountains of North America.
48373.m: The grizzly bear lives in the Rocky Mountains.

48374.q: Which big wild cat lives in the Rocky Mountains?
48374.e: The puma is a big wild cat with light brown fur. It lives in the mountains and forests of the Rocky Mountains and hunts deer there.
48374.m: The puma lives in the Rocky Mountains.

48375.q: Which animal with big curved horns climbs in the Rocky Mountains?
48375.e: The bighorn sheep has thick, curled horns. It climbs safely over steep rocks in North America. The ibex and chamois live in the Alps, the yak in Asia.
48375.m: The bighorn sheep climbs in the Rocky Mountains.

48376.q: Which national park in Canada is in the Rocky Mountains?
48376.e: Banff National Park is Canada's oldest national park. It lies right in the middle of the Rocky Mountains.
48376.m: Banff National Park is in the Canadian Rockies.

48377.q: Which large bird of prey is the national bird of the USA and also lives in the Rocky Mountains?
48377.e: The bald eagle has a white head and a yellow beak. It is the national bird of the USA.
48377.m: The bald eagle is the national bird of the USA.

48378.e: Kilimanjaro is in East Africa. It is the highest mountain in Africa.

a: In the high mountains of Nepal
In the rainforest on the Amazon
48380.e: The Sherpas live high up in the Himalayas, in Nepal. The highest mountains in the world are there.
48380.m: The Sherpas live in the mountains of Nepal.

48381.e: The highest point of Kilimanjaro is at 5895 metres. That makes it higher than any mountain in the Alps.

48382.q: What kind of mountain is Kilimanjaro?
48382.e: Kilimanjaro is a volcano. But it has not erupted for a very long time.

48383.q: What lies on the summit of Kilimanjaro, even though it is hot in Africa?
48383.e: At the top of the mountain it is very cold. So there is snow and glaciers there, even when it is hot below.
48383.m: There is snow at the top of Kilimanjaro.

48384.q: What is happening to the ice on Kilimanjaro?
a: There is less and less of it
There is more and more of it
48384.e: The glaciers on Kilimanjaro have been melting for many years. They have already become much smaller.
48384.m: The glaciers on Kilimanjaro are melting.

48385.q: Which animals do you often see in the savannah around Kilimanjaro?
48385.e: Around the mountain there is savannah with national parks. Elephants, for example, live there.

48386.q: How do most people get to the summit of Kilimanjaro?
48386.e: No railway goes up Kilimanjaro. Anyone who wants to reach the summit walks up over several days.

48387.q: On which continent are the Atlas Mountains?
48387.e: The Atlas Mountains are in the north-west of Africa. They are not far from Europe.
48387.m: The Atlas Mountains are in Africa.

48388.q: Which big city at the foot of the Atlas Mountains is famous for its market?
48388.e: Marrakesh is in Morocco near the High Atlas. On the big square Jemaa el-Fnaa there is a colourful market every day.
48388.m: Marrakesh lies at the foot of the Atlas Mountains.

48389.q: In which country is most of the Atlas Mountains?
48389.e: The Atlas Mountains stretch across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia. Most of them, and the highest peak, Toubkal, are in Morocco.
48389.m: Most of the Atlas Mountains are in Morocco.

48390.q: Which big desert lies south of the Atlas Mountains?
48390.e: The Atlas Mountains separate the coast in the north from the Sahara in the south. The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.
48390.m: The Sahara lies south of the Atlas Mountains.

48391.q: Who are the Atlas Mountains named after?
48391.e: Atlas is a giant from the old Greek myths. He is said to carry the sky on his shoulders.
48391.m: The Atlas Mountains are named after the giant Atlas.

48392.q: Which monkeys live in the forests of the Atlas Mountains?
48392.e: Barbary macaques live in the mountain forests of Morocco and Algeria. They have almost no tail.
48392.m: Barbary macaques live in the Atlas Mountains.

48393.q: Which people have lived in the Atlas Mountains for a very long time?
48393.e: The Berbers have lived in North Africa for a very long time. They call themselves Amazigh.
48393.m: Berbers live in the Atlas Mountains.

48394.q: Can snow fall in the Atlas Mountains in winter?
48394.e: Although the Atlas Mountains are in Africa, the high peaks are often white in winter. It is cold enough for snow there.
48394.m: Snow falls in the Atlas Mountains in winter too.

48395.q: In which country is Mount Fuji?
48395.e: Mount Fuji is in Japan. It is the highest mountain in the country.

48397.q: What kind of mountain is Mount Fuji?
a: A glacier mountain with no rock
48397.e: Mount Fuji is a volcano with an almost perfect cone shape. It last erupted in 1707 and is still considered active today.

48398.q: Roughly how high is Mount Fuji?
48398.e: Mount Fuji is 3776 metres high. That is lower than the Matterhorn.
48398.m: Mount Fuji is almost 3800 metres high.

48399.q: Which big city is not far from Mount Fuji?
48399.e: Mount Fuji is about 100 kilometres from Tokyo. On clear days you can see it from the city.
48399.m: On clear days you can see Mount Fuji from Tokyo.

48400.e: Mount Fuji looks like a large, almost even cone. That is why it is so famous.
48400.m: Mount Fuji is shaped like a cone.

48401.q: What does Mount Fuji often wear on its top in winter?
48401.e: In winter there is white snow on the summit of Mount Fuji. That is how it looks in many pictures.
48401.m: In winter Mount Fuji wears a white cap of snow.

48402.q: What is Mount Fuji to the people of Japan?
48402.e: Mount Fuji is a landmark of Japan. For many people it is a sacred mountain.
48402.m: Mount Fuji is a landmark of Japan.

a: Yes, many people hike up in summer
Only by train to the very top
48403.e: In summer many people climb Mount Fuji on foot. At the top they often watch the sunrise.
48403.m: In summer you can hike up Mount Fuji.

48404.q: In which city is Table Mountain?
48404.e: Table Mountain rises right behind the city of Cape Town. Cape Town is in South Africa.
48404.m: Table Mountain is in Cape Town.

48405.q: In which country is Table Mountain?
48405.e: Table Mountain rises behind the city of Cape Town. Cape Town is in South Africa.
48405.m: Table Mountain is in South Africa.

48406.q: Why is Table Mountain called that?
a: Its top is as flat as a table
It is pointed like a tower
It is round like a ball
48406.e: At the top the mountain is almost completely flat. It looks like a big table.
48406.m: Table Mountain is flat on top like a table.

48407.q: What is the cloud that often lies over Table Mountain called?
48407.e: A flat cloud often lies on the mountain and flows over the edge. People call it the ‘tablecloth’.
48407.m: The cloud on Table Mountain is called the tablecloth.

48408.q: How can you get up Table Mountain easily without walking?
48408.e: A cable car goes up Table Mountain. Its cabins turn round during the ride.
48408.m: A cable car goes up Table Mountain.

48409.q: Which sea can you see from Table Mountain?
48409.e: Cape Town is on the Atlantic Ocean. From Table Mountain you can see far out over the sea.
48409.m: From Table Mountain you can see the Atlantic.

48410.q: Roughly how high is Table Mountain near Cape Town?
48410.e: Table Mountain is a little over 1000 metres high. Because it rises right behind the city, it looks very mighty.
48410.m: Table Mountain is a little over 1000 metres high.

48411.q: Which birds live on a beach not far from Table Mountain?
48411.e: Not far from Table Mountain, African penguins live on a sandy beach. You can watch them there up close.

48412.q: What do we call a small, low mountain?
48412.e: A hill is a small rise in the land. It is much lower than a real mountain.
48412.m: A hill is a small, low mountain.

48413.q: What is the low land between two mountains called?
48413.e: Between mountains there is a valley. Often a stream or a river flows along the bottom of the valley.
48413.m: Between two mountains there is a valley.

48414.q: What is the sloping side of a mountain called?
48414.e: The slope is the sloping surface that leads from the summit down to the valley. A steep slope is hard to walk on.
48414.m: The sloping side of a mountain is called the slope.

48415.q: What is the lowest part of a mountain called?
48415.e: The mountain begins at its foot. From there it goes uphill to the summit.
48415.m: A mountain begins at its foot.

48416.q: What often flows along the bottom of a valley?
48416.e: Water always flows downhill. So streams gather in the valley to form a river.
48416.m: A river often flows along the bottom of a valley.

48417.q: What is a low point between mountains, where a path leads over into the next valley, called?
48417.e: A pass is a low point between mountains. A path or a road leads over it, for example over the Gotthard.
48417.m: You cross from one valley to another over a pass.

48418.q: Which religion do most Sherpas follow?
48418.e: Most Sherpas are Buddhists. In their villages there are monasteries and prayer flags.

48419.q: What is a long, narrow mountain crest with steep sides called?
48419.e: A ridge is a sharp edge at the top of a mountain. On the left and right it drops away steeply.
48419.m: A ridge is a narrow mountain crest.

48420.q: What stands on many mountain summits in Switzerland?
48420.e: On many summits in the Alps there is a cross. It shows that you have reached the top.
48420.m: A summit cross stands on many summits.

48421.q: Why is there often snow on high mountains?
a: It is colder at the top
It is warmer at the top
It never rains at the top
The sun never shines at the top
48421.e: The higher you go, the colder it gets. So the snow stays for a long time on high mountains.
48421.m: The higher you climb, the colder it gets.

48422.q: What is a large, slow stream of ice in the mountains called?
48422.e: A glacier forms from snow that turns into ice. The ice flows very slowly down the valley.
48422.m: A glacier is a slow river of ice.

48423.q: What is snow that suddenly slides down a slope called?
48423.e: An avalanche is a large amount of snow that thunders quickly down the slope. It is very dangerous.
48423.m: An avalanche is snow sliding down a slope.

48424.q: What is a snowflake made of?
48424.e: Snowflakes are made of tiny ice crystals. They form high up in cold clouds.
48424.m: Snowflakes are made of ice crystals.

48425.q: What is happening to many glaciers because the Earth is getting warmer?
48425.e: Because it is getting warmer, more ice melts than new ice forms. So many glaciers are getting smaller.
48425.m: Many glaciers are melting because it is getting warmer.

48426.q: How many arms does a typical snowflake have?
48426.e: The ice crystals grow in six directions. That is why a typical snowflake has six arms.
48426.m: A snowflake usually has six arms.

48427.q: What do ski tourers take with them in winter so that they can be found if there is an avalanche?
48427.e: An avalanche transceiver sends out signals. This helps rescuers find people buried in the snow more quickly.
48427.m: An avalanche transceiver helps to find buried people.

48428.q: What are the people in Nepal who accompany many climbers in the Himalayas called?
48428.e: The Sherpas live high in the mountains of Nepal. They know the mountains very well and help on expeditions.
48428.m: Sherpas accompany climbers in the Himalayas.

48429.q: Why can Sherpas work well high up in the mountains?
a: They are used to the thin air
48429.e: Sherpas have lived high in the mountains for many generations. Their bodies cope better with little oxygen.
48429.m: Sherpas are used to the thin mountain air.

48430.q: How many times has the Sherpa Kami Rita climbed Mount Everest (as of 2026)?
48430.e: In May 2026 Kami Rita stood on the summit for the 32nd time. No other person has been up there so often.
48430.m: Kami Rita has climbed Everest more often than anyone else.

48431.q: What do Sherpas often carry up the mountain for climbers?
48431.e: Sherpas carry tents, food and equipment to the camps on the mountain. Without them many expeditions would not be possible.
48431.m: Sherpas carry heavy loads for expeditions.

48432.q: What do climbers fix under their boots so they don't slip on ice?
48432.e: Crampons have sharp metal spikes. They grip the ice and give you a firm hold.
48432.m: Crampons give a good grip on ice.

48433.q: Why do climbers wear a helmet?
a: To protect them from falling rocks
48433.e: Rocks can fall down on a mountain. The helmet protects your head from them.
48433.m: A helmet protects you from falling rocks on a mountain.

48434.q: What is a house high in the mountains where climbers can spend the night called?
48434.e: In a mountain hut climbers can eat and sleep. In Switzerland the Swiss Alpine Club SAC runs many such huts.
48434.m: Climbers spend the night in a mountain hut.

48435.q: What is the big tent camp at the foot of a high mountain called?
48435.e: Climbers stay at base camp before they set off for the summit. From there they start their climb.
48435.m: Climbers set off for the summit from base camp.

48436.q: What do climbers use to secure each other so that nobody falls?
48436.e: Climbers tie themselves together with a strong rope. If one of them slips, the others hold on.
48436.m: A rope protects climbers from falling.

48437.q: Which climber from South Tyrol climbed Mount Everest in 1978 without bottled oxygen?
48437.e: In 1978 Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler were the first to climb Everest without oxygen from bottles.
48437.m: Reinhold Messner climbed Everest without bottled oxygen.

48438.q: What should you do first on a mountain when a thunderstorm is coming?
48438.e: In a thunderstorm lightning often strikes high points. So you should leave summits and ridges quickly.
48438.m: In a thunderstorm you leave summits and ridges.

48440.q: What is the job of people who lead guests safely up mountains called?
48440.e: Mountain guides know the routes, the weather and the dangers on the mountain. In Switzerland they do a long training for this.
48440.m: A mountain guide leads guests safely up mountains.

48441.q: What is the channel through which magma rises in a volcano called?
48441.e: The vent is like a chimney inside the volcano. Magma rises up through it from deep below.
48441.m: Magma rises up through the vent.

48442.q: Where does magma collect deep under a volcano?
48442.e: Deep under the volcano there is a large space full of magma. It is called the magma chamber.
48442.m: The magma chamber lies under the volcano.

48443.q: Which Roman god is the volcano named after?
48443.e: For the Romans, Vulcan was the god of fire and blacksmiths. The word volcano comes from his name.
48443.m: The word volcano comes from the fire god Vulcan.

48444.q: What is the cone of a volcano made of?
48444.e: With every eruption new layers of lava and ash settle on the mountain. This is how the volcanic cone grows.
48444.m: A volcanic cone grows layer by layer.

48445.q: What does a shield volcano look like?
48445.e: A shield volcano forms from runny lava that flows a long way. So it is wide and flat like a shield lying down.
48445.m: A shield volcano is wide and flat.

48446.q: Which volcano in Italy is the highest active volcano in Europe?
48446.e: Etna is on the island of Sicily. It is over 3000 metres high and erupts often.
48446.m: Etna on Sicily is Europe's highest active volcano.

48447.q: What do we call a volcano that will never erupt again?
48447.e: An extinct volcano has been dead for a very long time and will not erupt again. A dormant volcano, on the other hand, can wake up again.
48447.m: An extinct volcano does not erupt any more.

48448.q: What is liquid rock that flows out of a volcano called?
48448.e: As soon as the hot, liquid rock reaches the Earth's surface, it is called lava. It flows down the mountain.
48448.m: Liquid rock on the surface is called lava.

48450.q: What colour is very hot, fresh lava?
48450.e: Fresh lava is so hot that it glows red and orange. When it cools, it turns dark.
48450.m: Hot lava glows red and orange.

48451.q: What happens to lava when it cools down?
48451.e: Cooled lava becomes solid. This forms new rock, for example basalt.

48452.q: Which light volcanic stone can float on water?
48452.e: Pumice is full of tiny air holes. That makes it so light that it floats on water.
48452.m: Pumice floats because it is full of air holes.

48453.q: What is the black, shiny volcanic glass called?
48453.e: Obsidian forms when lava cools very quickly. It is black, shiny and has sharp edges.
48453.m: Obsidian is black glass made from lava.

48454.q: What can smooth lava look like once it has cooled?
48454.e: Smooth lava has a skin that folds as it flows. When it hardens, it looks like twisted ropes.
48454.m: Smooth lava can look like twisted ropes.

48455.q: Why can you hardly walk barefoot on rough, cooled lava?
48455.e: Rough lava is full of pointed, sharp lumps. Walking on it hurts your feet.
48455.m: Rough lava is sharp and jagged.

48456.q: What is liquid rock called while it is still deep inside the Earth?
48456.e: Under the ground the melted rock is called magma. The word comes from Greek and means ‘kneaded mass’.
48456.m: Under the ground liquid rock is called magma.

a: It is lighter than the rock around it
It is heavier than the rock around it
It is washed up by water
It is sucked up by the wind
48457.e: Hot magma is lighter than the solid rock around it. So it slowly rises, like an air bubble in water.
48457.m: Magma rises because it is lighter.

48458.q: Which layer of the Earth does magma come from?
48458.e: Below the Earth's crust is the mantle. It is so hot there that rock can melt.
48458.m: Magma forms deep in the Earth's mantle.

48459.q: Apart from rock, what else is dissolved in magma?
48459.e: Magma contains lots of gases, for example water vapour. They are dissolved in it like the fizz in a bottle of sparkling water.
48459.m: Gases in magma build up pressure.

48460.q: Which rock forms when magma cools slowly deep inside the Earth?
48460.e: When magma cools very slowly underground, granite with large grains forms. Granite is also found in the Swiss Alps.
48460.m: Granite is hardened magma from deep down.

48461.q: What do researchers often notice when magma rises under a volcano?
a: The ground rises and shakes slightly
The water in the lakes freezes
48461.e: Rising magma pushes the ground up and makes it shake slightly. Measuring instruments show this, so people can be warned before an eruption.

48462.e: Magma is melted rock. It is very hot and so it is liquid like thick porridge.

48463.q: What happens when too much magma and gas collect under a volcano?
48463.e: Magma and gas push upwards harder and harder. When the pressure gets too great, the volcano erupts.
48463.m: Too much pressure leads to a volcanic eruption.

48464.q: What is the crater of a volcano?
a: The opening at the top of the volcano
A river next to the volcano
48464.e: The crater is the opening at the top of the volcano. That is where the lava comes out during an eruption.
48464.m: The crater is at the top of the volcano.

48465.q: What shape is a crater usually?
48465.e: A crater is a round hollow. It looks like a big bowl.
48465.m: A crater looks like a bowl.

48466.q: What do we call a lake in an old volcanic crater?
48466.e: When a volcano is extinct, rainwater can collect in the crater. This makes a crater lake.
48466.m: A lake can form in the crater of an old volcano.

48467.q: What is a huge hollow that forms when a volcano collapses in on itself called?
48467.e: After a big eruption the magma chamber is empty. The mountain collapses, and a huge hollow forms: the caldera.
48467.m: A caldera is a collapsed volcanic hollow.

48468.q: Where do the many craters on the moon come from?
48468.e: Most moon craters formed when lumps of rock from space crashed onto the moon. Such craters are called impact craters.
48468.m: Moon craters are made by impacts.

48469.q: What is a smaller crater on the side of a volcano called?
48469.e: Sometimes the magma finds a way out on the side of the mountain. A side crater forms there.
48469.m: A side crater can form on the side of a volcano.

48470.q: What often rises from a crater even when the volcano is not erupting?
48470.e: Even a quiet volcano often gives off gases and steam. Lava and glowing rocks only come out during an eruption.

48471.q: Which language does the word ‘crater’ come from?
48471.e: For the ancient Greeks a krater was a large vessel in which wine was mixed with water. Later the name was also given to the opening at the top of a volcano.
48471.m: The word crater comes from Greek.

48472.q: Which city was buried by Vesuvius in the year 79?
48472.e: In the year 79 AD Vesuvius erupted. Ash buried the Roman city of Pompeii.
48472.m: Vesuvius buried the city of Pompeii.

48473.q: What is a scientist who studies volcanoes called?
48473.e: Volcanologists watch volcanoes and measure things such as gases and temperature. This lets them warn people about eruptions.

48474.q: What flies high into the sky during a volcanic eruption?
48474.e: During an eruption rock is torn apart into fine ash. It can rise many kilometres into the sky.
48474.m: A volcano can hurl ash high into the sky.

48475.q: Which volcano in Iceland stopped many flights in Europe in 2010 with its ash cloud?
48475.e: The ash from the Icelandic volcano drifted across Europe. Planes were not allowed to fly for days, including in Switzerland.
48475.m: Volcanic ash can stop air traffic.

48476.q: What happened in Switzerland in 1816 after a huge volcanic eruption in Indonesia?
48476.e: In 1815 the volcano Tambora erupted. Its ash cooled the Earth, and 1816 was cold and wet in Switzerland; many people went hungry.
48476.m: A volcano can change the weather all over the world.

48477.q: What are lumps of lava that are hurled through the air called?
48477.e: During an eruption lumps of lava fly through the air. They cool as they fly and are called volcanic bombs.
48477.m: Volcanic bombs are flying lumps of lava.

48478.q: Which volcano in Italy is called the ‘Lighthouse of the Mediterranean’?
48478.e: Stromboli has been erupting almost constantly with small eruptions for a very long time. At night its glow can be seen far across the sea.
48478.m: Stromboli glows at night like a lighthouse.

48479.q: Why do plants often grow well on volcanic soil?
a: Volcanic ash makes the soil fertile
48479.e: Volcanic ash contains lots of minerals. Over time it turns into fertile soil, for example for grapevines on Etna.
48479.m: Volcanic ash makes the soil fertile.

48480.q: What should people do when a volcano near them erupts?
a: Put the lava out with water
48480.e: During an eruption the authorities tell people where to go. You get to safety and keep your distance.
48480.m: During an eruption you get to safety.

48481.q: Which ocean does the Ring of Fire go around?
48481.e: The Ring of Fire runs all around the Pacific Ocean. That is why it is also called the Pacific Ring of Fire.
48481.m: The Ring of Fire lies around the Pacific.

48482.q: Why is the Pacific Ring of Fire called that?
a: There are very many volcanoes there
The sun shines most strongly there
48482.e: Around the Pacific there are very many volcanoes, as if on a chain. That is why people speak of a ring of fire.
48482.m: The Ring of Fire is a chain of volcanoes.

48483.q: Roughly what shape is the Pacific Ring of Fire?
48483.e: The Ring of Fire is not completely closed. It is roughly the shape of a horseshoe.
48483.m: The Ring of Fire is shaped like a horseshoe.

48485.q: Apart from volcanoes, what happens especially often along the Pacific Ring of Fire?
48485.e: The Earth shakes very often along the Ring of Fire. About 90 out of 100 earthquakes in the world happen there.
48485.m: The Earth often shakes along the Ring of Fire.

48486.q: What meets along the Pacific Ring of Fire?
48486.e: The Earth's crust is made up of large plates. Along the Ring of Fire they collide, or one plate pushes under another.
48486.m: Tectonic plates collide along the Ring of Fire.

48487.q: Which famous volcano on the Ring of Fire is the highest mountain in Japan?
48487.e: Mount Fuji is a volcano and, at 3776 metres, the highest mountain in Japan. It has a beautiful cone shape.
48487.m: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain.

48488.q: How many of the world's active volcanoes lie on the Pacific Ring of Fire?
48488.e: About two thirds of all active volcanoes on Earth lie on the Pacific Ring of Fire. That is clearly more than half.
48488.m: Most active volcanoes lie on the Ring of Fire.

48489.q: How did the islands of Hawaii form?
a: From a piece of mainland that broke off
48489.e: Volcanoes on the seabed erupted again and again. The lava piled up until islands rose out of the water.
48489.m: Hawaii is made up of volcanic islands.

48490.q: In which ocean are the islands of Hawaii?
48490.e: Hawaii lies in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. The islands are far away from any mainland.
48490.m: Hawaii lies in the middle of the Pacific.

48491.q: Which country does Hawaii belong to?
48491.e: Hawaii is a state of the USA. It is the only one made up entirely of islands.
48491.m: Hawaii is a state of the USA.

48492.q: What is the very active volcano on the Big Island of Hawaii called?
48492.e: Kilauea is one of the most active volcanoes in the world. It is in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park.
48492.m: Kilauea on Hawaii is very active.

48493.q: Which volcano on Hawaii is the largest active volcano on Earth?
48493.e: Mauna Loa is a huge shield volcano. Measured by its mass, it is the largest active volcano in the world.
48493.m: Mauna Loa is the largest active volcano.

48494.q: In the legends of Hawaii, what is the goddess of volcanoes called?
48494.e: According to the old legends of Hawaii, the goddess Pele lives in a volcanic crater on the Big Island. She is the goddess of fire and volcanoes.
48494.m: Pele is the volcano goddess of Hawaii.

48495.q: What happens when lava flows into the sea on Hawaii?
48495.e: The lava cools in the water and turns into new rock. This is how the island grows bit by bit.
48495.m: Lava in the sea makes the island bigger.

48496.q: Which mountain on Hawaii is over 10,000 metres high when measured from the seabed?
48496.e: Mauna Kea rises over 4000 metres out of the sea. But a large part of it is under water; altogether it is over 10,000 metres.
48496.m: Measured from the seabed, Mauna Kea is enormous.

a: A spring that shoots up hot water
A lake with lots of fish
48497.e: A geyser is a hot spring. Again and again it shoots a fountain of hot water and steam into the air.
48497.m: A geyser shoots hot water into the air.

48498.q: In which country is the geyser that all geysers are named after?
48498.e: The ‘Great Geysir’ is in Iceland. All the other spouting springs in the world were named after it.
48498.m: The word geyser comes from Iceland.

48499.q: What heats up the water of a geyser?
48499.e: Under a geyser there is hot rock, often close to magma. It heats the water in the ground.
48499.m: Hot rock deep down heats the geyser.

48500.q: What pushes the water up out of a geyser?
48500.e: Down below the water gets so hot that it turns into steam. The steam pushes the water above it up hard.
48500.m: Steam pushes the water out of the geyser.

48501.q: What is the famous geyser in Yellowstone National Park in the USA called?
48501.e: Old Faithful shoots up very regularly, so visitors can almost wait for it.
48501.m: Old Faithful is a famous geyser in the USA.

48502.q: What makes the Strokkur geyser in Iceland so well known?
a: It erupts only once a year
It shoots out ice cold water
48502.e: Strokkur shoots its water up about every ten minutes. So almost every visitor sees it in action.
48502.m: Strokkur in Iceland erupts every few minutes.

48503.q: Which national park has the most geysers in the world?
48503.e: Yellowstone National Park in the USA has more geysers than anywhere else. There is a lot of hot magma under the park.
48503.m: Yellowstone has the most geysers in the world.

48504.q: Why must you not get too close to a geyser?
48504.e: The water of a geyser is as hot as boiling water. You can get badly scalded.

a: Warm water that comes out of the ground
Water that you heat in a saucepan
48505.e: At a hot spring, water comes warm out of the Earth. It was heated deep down by the Earth's heat.
48505.m: A hot spring comes warm out of the Earth.

48506.q: What is another name for a hot spring?
48506.e: The word ‘thermal’ means warm. That is why hot springs are also called thermal springs.
48506.m: A hot spring is also called a thermal spring.

48507.q: In which town in Aargau did the Romans already bathe in hot springs?
48507.e: The Romans called the place Aquae Helveticae. The thermal springs of Baden are still used today.
48507.m: The Romans already bathed in Baden.

48508.q: Which place in Valais is known for its hot springs?
48508.e: Leukerbad is in Valais and is famous for its thermal water. Many people bathe there in warm pools.
48508.m: Leukerbad in Valais has hot springs.

48509.q: Which animals in Japan like to bathe in hot springs in winter?
48509.e: Snow monkeys, the Japanese macaques, live in Japan. In the cold winter they warm up in hot springs.
48509.m: In Japan snow monkeys bathe in hot springs.

48510.q: What is a bath in a hot spring in Japan called?
48510.e: There are very many hot springs in Japan. A bath in one is called an onsen.
48510.m: In Japan a hot spring bath is called an onsen.

48511.q: Through which gorge does the warm spring water flow to Bad Ragaz?
48511.e: The warm spring of Bad Ragaz rises in the Tamina Gorge. From there the water is piped to the village.
48511.m: The thermal water of Bad Ragaz comes from the Tamina Gorge.

48512.q: Which place in Turkey has white terraces made by hot springs?
48512.e: In Pamukkale warm water full of lime flows over the hillside. The lime forms white pools that look like snow.

a: Strong wind presses on the ground
Lots of rain makes the ground soft
48513.e: The Earth's crust is made up of large plates. When they suddenly shift, the Earth shakes.
48513.m: Earthquakes happen when tectonic plates move.

48514.q: Where should you take cover indoors during an earthquake?
48514.e: Under a sturdy table you are protected from falling objects. Windows can break and lifts can get stuck.
48514.m: In an earthquake you take cover under a sturdy table.

48515.q: Which Swiss city was destroyed by a strong earthquake in 1356?
48515.e: The Basel earthquake of 1356 was one of the strongest in Central Europe. Many houses collapsed or burned.

48516.q: In which canton does the Earth shake most often in Switzerland?
48516.e: Valais has the most earthquakes in Switzerland. This has to do with how the Alps formed.
48516.m: Valais has the most Swiss earthquakes.

48517.q: What are the smaller quakes that follow a big earthquake called?
48517.e: After a strong earthquake the Earth often shakes several more times. These tremors are called aftershocks.
48517.m: A big quake is often followed by aftershocks.

48518.q: What is the place on the Earth's surface directly above the centre of an earthquake called?
48518.e: An earthquake starts deep in the Earth. The point directly above it on the surface is called the epicentre.
48518.m: The epicentre lies above the centre of the earthquake.

48519.q: Which organisation in Switzerland monitors earthquakes?
48519.e: The Swiss Seismological Service is part of ETH Zurich. It measures all earthquakes in Switzerland.
48519.m: The Swiss Seismological Service measures earthquakes.

48520.q: Which language does the word tsunami come from?
48520.e: Tsunami is a Japanese word. It means ‘harbour wave’.

48521.q: What can be a warning sign of a tsunami on the beach?
48521.e: Sometimes the water draws back a long way before a tsunami. Then you must leave the beach at once.
48521.m: If the sea suddenly pulls back, you must get away.

48522.q: Where should you go when there is a tsunami warning?
a: Onto a hill or somewhere high up
Onto a boat on the beach
48522.e: The wave floods low land. On a hill or in a tall, solid building you are safer.
48522.m: In a tsunami warning you go somewhere high up.

48523.q: How fast can a tsunami travel on the open sea?
48523.e: In the deep sea a tsunami can travel at many hundreds of kilometres per hour. That is about as fast as a plane.
48523.m: A tsunami races across the sea as fast as a plane.

48524.q: When does a tsunami wave become especially high?
a: When it is in the middle of the sea
48524.e: In the deep sea the wave is flat and hard to see. Only in the shallow water at the coast does it tower up high.
48524.m: At the coast a tsunami towers up high.

48525.q: On which day in 2004 did a huge tsunami hit the coasts of the Indian Ocean?
48525.e: On the day after Christmas 2004 a strong undersea earthquake near Indonesia set off a tsunami. It hit many countries around the Indian Ocean.
48525.m: The great Indian Ocean tsunami came on 26 December 2004.

48526.q: In which Swiss lake was there a huge flood wave in the year 563?
48526.e: In 563 a mountainside collapsed at the eastern end of Lake Geneva. This set off a flood wave that reached Geneva.
48526.m: A lake can have a flood wave too.

48527.q: In which country is the volcano Popocatépetl?
48527.e: Popocatépetl is in Mexico. It is about 70 kilometres from the capital, Mexico City.

48528.q: What does the name Popocatépetl mean?
48528.e: The name comes from the old Nahuatl language. It means ‘smoking mountain’, because smoke often rises from it.

48529.q: What often rises from the volcano Popocatépetl in Mexico?
48529.e: Popocatépetl is an active volcano. Smoke and ash often rise from its crater. People call it ‘El Popo’ for short.

48530.e: Popocatépetl is over 5000 metres high. That makes it higher than any mountain in Switzerland.
48530.m: Popocatépetl is higher than all Swiss mountains.

48532.q: What often lies on the summit of Popocatépetl because it is so high?
48532.e: Popocatépetl is over 5000 metres high. Up there it is so cold that there is often snow on the summit.
48532.m: There is often snow on high Popocatépetl.

48533.q: What does the active volcano Popocatépetl keep giving off?
48533.e: Popocatépetl has been active again since 1994. It often gives off ash and smoke, sometimes as far as Mexico City.
48533.m: Popocatépetl smokes and spits out ash.

48534.q: What type of volcano is Popocatépetl?
48534.e: Popocatépetl is built up of many layers of lava and ash. That gives it its typical steep cone shape.

48535.q: Roughly how long is the Nile?
48535.e: The Nile is about 6650 kilometres long. That is more than five times as long as the Rhine.
48535.m: The Nile is about 6650 kilometres long.

48536.q: On which continent does the Nile flow?
48536.e: The Nile flows from south to north in the east of Africa.
48536.m: The Nile is a river in Africa.

48537.q: What is the big dam on the Nile in Egypt called?
48537.e: The Aswan Dam holds back the Nile to form a huge lake. It protects against floods and produces electricity.
48537.m: The Aswan Dam holds back the Nile.

48538.q: Which country is especially known for the Nile and its pyramids?
48538.e: In ancient Egypt people lived along the banks of the Nile. The famous pyramids are nearby too.
48538.m: Ancient Egypt lay along the Nile.

48539.q: What are the two rivers that join to form the Nile called?
48539.e: The White Nile comes from East Africa, the Blue Nile from Ethiopia. Where they meet, the Nile itself begins.
48539.m: The White and Blue Nile join to become the Nile.

48540.q: Which dangerous animal lives in the Nile?
48540.e: The Nile crocodile is named after the river. It is one of the largest crocodiles.
48540.m: The Nile crocodile lives in the Nile.

48541.q: What did the Nile floods bring onto the fields every year in the past?
48541.e: When the Nile burst its banks, fertile mud was left behind. Grain grew especially well in it.
48541.m: The mud of the Nile made the fields fertile.

48542.q: Which big city is on the Nile?
48542.e: Cairo is the capital of Egypt. It lies right on the Nile.

48543.q: What is the big city in the middle of the Amazon rainforest called?
48543.e: Manaus is in Brazil on the Amazon, in the middle of the rainforest. Many goods arrive in the city by ship.
48543.m: Manaus lies in the middle of the Amazon rainforest.

48544.q: Which big wild cat hunts on the banks of the Amazon?
48544.e: The jaguar is the largest wild cat in the Americas. It swims well and often hunts by the water, even caimans.
48544.m: The jaguar hunts along the Amazon.

48545.q: Which huge snake lives in the Amazon region?
48545.e: The green anaconda lives in the rivers and swamps of the Amazon. It is one of the heaviest snakes in the world.
48545.m: The anaconda lives along the Amazon.

48546.q: What kind of forest grows around the Amazon?
48546.e: The largest rainforest on Earth is along the Amazon. Very many kinds of animals and plants live there.
48546.m: The largest rainforest on Earth grows along the Amazon.

48547.q: Which fish with sharp teeth lives in the Amazon?
48547.e: Piranhas live in the rivers of South America. They have very sharp teeth.

48548.q: Which special colour is the Amazon river dolphin often?
48548.e: The Amazon river dolphin is also called the pink river dolphin. Older animals in particular are often pink.
48548.m: Pink dolphins live in the Amazon.

48549.q: Which sea does the Amazon flow into?
48549.e: The Amazon flows into the Atlantic Ocean in Brazil.
48549.m: The Amazon flows into the Atlantic.

48550.q: How many bridges cross the main stream of the Amazon?
48550.e: Not a single bridge crosses the main stream of the Amazon. People cross it by boat and ferry.
48550.m: You cross the Amazon by boat, not by bridge.

48551.q: In which country does the Mississippi flow?
48551.e: The Mississippi flows right through the middle of the United States of America.
48551.m: The Mississippi is a big river in the USA.

48552.q: Which sea does the Mississippi flow into?
48552.e: The Mississippi flows from north to south. Near New Orleans it flows into the Gulf of Mexico.
48552.m: The Mississippi flows into the Gulf of Mexico.

48553.q: Which well-known city lies near the mouth of the Mississippi?
48553.e: New Orleans lies just before the mouth of the Mississippi. The city is known for its jazz music.
48553.m: New Orleans is on the lower Mississippi.

48554.q: Which ships with big paddle wheels used to sail on the Mississippi?
48554.e: Paddle steamers are driven by big paddle wheels. In the past they carried people and goods up and down the river.
48554.m: Paddle steamers used to sail on the Mississippi.

48555.q: Which boy from a famous book lives by the Mississippi?
48555.e: Mark Twain wrote ‘The Adventures of Tom Sawyer’. Tom lives in a small town on the Mississippi.
48555.m: Tom Sawyer has his adventures by the Mississippi.

48556.q: What does the name Mississippi mean in a Native American language?
48556.e: The name comes from the Ojibwe language. It means roughly ‘great river’.

48557.q: Which big river flows into the Mississippi?
48557.e: The Missouri is the longest tributary of the Mississippi. It flows into the Mississippi near St Louis.
48557.m: The Missouri flows into the Mississippi.

48558.q: In which country does the Yangtze flow?
48558.e: The Yangtze flows from west to east right across China to the sea.
48558.m: The Yangtze is a river in China.

48559.q: Which river is the longest river in Asia?
48559.e: The Yangtze is about 6300 kilometres long. That makes it the longest river in Asia.
48559.m: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.

48560.q: Which huge city lies at the mouth of the Yangtze?
48560.e: The Yangtze flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai. Shanghai is one of the biggest cities in the world.
48560.m: Shanghai lies at the mouth of the Yangtze.

48561.q: What is the huge dam on the Yangtze called?
48561.e: The Three Gorges Dam holds back the Yangtze. Its power station is one of the largest in the world.
48561.m: The Three Gorges Dam is on the Yangtze.

48562.q: What does the power station at the Three Gorges Dam produce?
48562.e: The dammed water drives large turbines. This produces a great deal of electricity.
48562.m: The water of the Yangtze produces electricity.

48563.e: The Yangtze rises high up on the Tibetan Plateau. From there it flows east.

48564.q: What place does the Yangtze have among the longest rivers in the world?
48564.e: Only the Nile and the Amazon are longer than the Yangtze.
48564.m: The Yangtze is the third longest river in the world.

48565.q: In which country does most of the Ganges flow?
48565.e: The Ganges flows through the north of India. At the end it reaches Bangladesh.
48565.m: The Ganges flows mainly through India.

48566.q: For which religion is the Ganges a holy river?
48566.e: The Ganges is holy for Hindus. Many bathe in it because they believe the water cleanses the soul.
48566.m: The Ganges is holy for Hindus.

48567.q: Which mountain range does the water of the Ganges come from?
48567.e: The Ganges rises at a glacier in the Himalayas. That is the highest mountain range in the world.
48567.m: The Ganges comes from the Himalayas.

48568.q: What do many people in India do in the holy river Ganges?
a: They pan for gold in it
They dive for pearls in it
48568.e: For many people in India the Ganges is holy. They bathe in it because they believe the water makes them pure.
48568.m: Many people bathe in the holy Ganges.

48569.q: Which well-known holy city lies on the Ganges?
48569.e: Varanasi is one of the oldest cities in India. There people walk down wide steps to the river.
48569.m: Varanasi is a holy city on the Ganges.

48570.q: Which big wild cat lives in the forests along the Ganges?
48570.e: Where the Ganges flows into the sea, a large forest grows in the water. Tigers live there. They are good swimmers.

48571.q: Which bay does the Ganges flow into?
48571.e: Together with the Brahmaputra, the Ganges flows into the Bay of Bengal in Bangladesh.
48571.m: The Ganges flows into the Bay of Bengal.

48572.q: On which continent does the Mekong flow?
48572.e: The Mekong flows through South-East Asia.
48572.m: The Mekong is a river in Asia.

48573.q: Through how many countries does the Mekong flow?
48573.e: The Mekong flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.
48573.m: The Mekong flows through six countries.

48574.q: In which country does the Mekong flow into the sea?
48574.e: In the south of Vietnam the Mekong splits into many branches. This area is called the Mekong Delta.
48574.m: The Mekong reaches the sea in Vietnam.

48575.q: What do traders sell at the floating markets on the Mekong?
48575.e: In the Mekong Delta traders sell fruit and vegetables straight from their boats.
48575.m: There are floating markets on the Mekong.

48576.q: Which plant is grown especially widely in the Mekong Delta?
48576.e: A great deal of rice grows in the damp, warm Mekong Delta. It is also called Vietnam's rice bowl.
48576.m: Lots of rice grows in the Mekong Delta.

48577.q: A giant fish lives in the Mekong. What kind of fish is it?
48577.e: The Mekong giant catfish can grow to about 3 metres long. It is one of the largest river fish. Sharks, tuna and swordfish live in the sea.
48577.m: The huge Mekong giant catfish lives in the Mekong.

48578.e: The Mekong begins high up in Tibet in China. Then it flows south.

48579.q: Which great apes live only south of the River Congo?
48579.e: Bonobos live only in the rainforest south of the Congo. They cannot swim, so the wide river is a boundary for them.
48579.m: Bonobos live only south of the Congo.

48580.q: What world record does the Congo hold?
48580.e: In some places the Congo is over 200 metres deep. No other river is so deep.
48580.m: The Congo is the deepest river in the world.

48581.q: How many times does the Congo cross the equator?
48581.e: The Congo flows in a big curve. On the way it crosses the equator twice.
48581.m: The Congo crosses the equator twice.

48582.q: Which river in Africa carries the most water?
48582.e: The Congo flows through an area where it rains a great deal. So it carries more water than any other river in Africa, even more than the Nile.
48582.m: The Congo carries the most water of all rivers in Africa.

48583.q: Which two capital cities face each other across the River Congo?
48583.e: Kinshasa and Brazzaville face each other across the Congo. Only the river separates the two capitals.
48583.m: Two capitals face each other across the Congo.

48584.q: What has the same name as the River Congo?
48584.e: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo bear the name of the river.
48584.m: Two countries are named like the River Congo.

48585.q: Which sea does the Congo flow into?
48585.e: The Congo flows into the Atlantic Ocean on the west coast of Africa.
48585.m: The Congo flows into the Atlantic.

48586.q: What do we call the place where a river begins?
48586.e: At the source, the water comes out of the ground or out of a glacier. That is where the river begins.
48586.m: A river begins at its source.

48587.q: In which country is the source of the Rhine?
48587.e: The Rhine rises in the canton of the Grisons. Then it flows all the way to the North Sea.

48588.e: The Rhône comes out of the Rhône Glacier in Valais. The glacier is near the Furka Pass.
48588.m: The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier.

48589.q: Which way does the water of a river always flow?
48589.e: Water always flows from higher to lower ground. So the source is higher than the mouth.

a: A river that flows into another
48590.e: A tributary flows into a larger river. The Aare, for example, is a tributary of the Rhine.
48590.m: A tributary flows into a larger river.

48591.q: Where is the water of a river usually coldest?
48591.e: Near the source the water often comes from a glacier or from the ground. There it is still very cold.
48591.m: At the source river water is usually very cold.

48592.q: What do we call a small flowing body of water that often comes from a spring?
48592.e: From many springs a small stream flows first. Later several streams join to become a river.
48592.m: A stream often flows first from a spring.

48593.q: What do we call the place where a river ends?
48593.e: At the mouth a river flows into a sea, a lake or another river.
48593.m: A river ends at its mouth.

48594.q: Which lake does the Rhine flow into before it reaches Schaffhausen?
48594.e: The Alpine Rhine flows into the eastern end of Lake Constance. Then it continues to Schaffhausen.
48594.m: The Rhine flows through Lake Constance.

48595.q: What is a river mouth where the river splits into many branches called?
48595.e: In a delta the river splits into many small branches before it reaches the sea.
48595.m: A delta is a river mouth with many branches.

48596.q: What is the delta named after?
48596.e: Delta is a letter of the Greek alphabet. Many river mouths look similar to this letter.
48596.m: The delta is named after a Greek letter.

48597.q: Which lake does the Rhône flow into after Valais?
48597.e: The Rhône flows through the whole of Valais. At Le Bouveret it flows into Lake Geneva.
48597.m: The Rhône flows into Lake Geneva.

48598.q: Which Italian river does the Ticino flow into?
48598.e: The Ticino flows through Lake Maggiore into Italy. Near Pavia it flows into the Po.
48598.m: The Ticino flows into the Po.

48599.q: What does the water often taste like where a river flows into the sea?
48599.e: At the mouth the fresh water of the river mixes with the salt water of the sea. That is why it is only slightly salty there.
48599.m: At the mouth river water mixes with sea water.

48600.q: Between which two countries are Niagara Falls?
48600.e: Niagara Falls lie exactly on the border between the USA and Canada.
48600.m: Niagara Falls lie between the USA and Canada.

48601.q: On which continent are Niagara Falls?
48601.e: The USA and Canada are in North America, and that is where Niagara Falls are too.
48601.m: Niagara Falls are in North America.

48602.q: What is the largest of the Niagara Falls called because of its shape?
48602.e: The largest fall is curved like a horseshoe. That is why it is called Horseshoe Falls.
48602.m: The largest Niagara fall is called Horseshoe Falls.

48603.q: Between which two lakes does the Niagara River flow?
48603.e: The Niagara River connects Lake Erie with Lake Ontario. On the way it plunges over Niagara Falls.
48603.m: The Niagara flows from Lake Erie into Lake Ontario.

48604.q: How many waterfalls together make up Niagara Falls?
48604.e: Niagara Falls are made up of Horseshoe Falls, American Falls and Bridal Veil Falls.
48604.m: Niagara Falls are made up of three falls.

48605.q: How do tourists get really close to Niagara Falls?
48605.e: Tour boats go right up close to the roaring falls. The passengers are given raincoats because they get wet.
48605.m: You can go close to Niagara Falls by boat.

48606.q: Roughly how high are Horseshoe Falls at Niagara?
48606.e: Horseshoe Falls are about 50 metres high. They are not very high, but very wide with lots of water.
48606.m: Horseshoe Falls are about 50 metres high.

48607.q: On which continent are Victoria Falls?
48607.e: Victoria Falls are in southern Africa.

48608.q: Which river plunges down at Victoria Falls?
48608.e: The Zambezi flows through southern Africa. At Victoria Falls it drops over a wide rocky edge.

48609.q: On the border of which two countries are Victoria Falls?
48609.e: Victoria Falls lie exactly on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
48609.m: Victoria Falls lie between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

48610.q: Who are Victoria Falls named after?
48610.e: The explorer David Livingstone named the falls after the British Queen Victoria.
48610.m: Victoria Falls bear the name of Queen Victoria.

48611.q: What does the African name of Victoria Falls mean?
48611.e: Local people call the falls Mosi-oa-Tunya. That means ‘the smoke that thunders’, because spray rises and it roars loudly.
48611.m: In a local language Victoria Falls are called ‘the smoke that thunders’.

48612.q: Roughly how wide are Victoria Falls?
48612.e: Victoria Falls are about 1.7 kilometres wide. The water falls into a gorge along this whole width.
48612.m: Victoria Falls are almost two kilometres wide.

48613.q: What can you often see in the spray of Victoria Falls when the sun is shining?
48613.e: The tiny droplets of spray split the sunlight. This often makes a rainbow.
48613.m: A rainbow often shines over Victoria Falls.

48614.q: Roughly how far does the water drop at Victoria Falls?
48614.e: The water drops about 108 metres into a narrow gorge.
48614.m: At Victoria Falls the water drops about 100 metres.

48615.q: On which continent are the Iguazú Falls?
48615.e: The Iguazú Falls are in the rainforest of South America.
48615.m: The Iguazú Falls are in South America.

48616.q: Between which two countries are the Iguazú Falls?
48616.e: Here the Iguazú River forms the border between Argentina and Brazil.
48616.m: The Iguazú Falls lie between Argentina and Brazil.

48617.q: Roughly how many separate falls make up the Iguazú Falls?
48617.e: The Iguazú Falls are made up of about 275 separate waterfalls. Together they are almost 3 kilometres wide.
48617.m: Iguazú is made up of about 275 waterfalls.

48618.q: What is the largest part of the Iguazú Falls called?
48618.e: The Devil's Throat is a U-shaped gorge. That is where the most water plunges down.
48618.m: The largest fall at Iguazú is called the Devil's Throat.

48619.q: What does the word Iguazú mean?
48619.e: The word comes from the Guaraní language. It means ‘big water’.

48620.q: Which animal with a long nose do you often see at the Iguazú Falls?
48620.e: Coatis live in the rainforest around the falls. They often come close to visitors.
48620.m: Lots of coatis live at Iguazú.

48621.q: What kind of forest surrounds the Iguazú Falls?
48621.e: Dense rainforest grows around the waterfalls. Both countries have a national park there.
48621.m: The Iguazú Falls are in the rainforest.

48622.q: Which waterfall is considered the highest in the world?
48622.e: Angel Falls plunge almost a kilometre down. They are considered the highest waterfall on Earth.
48622.m: Angel Falls are considered the highest waterfall in the world.

48623.q: How do visitors usually get to Angel Falls?
48623.e: No road leads to Angel Falls. You travel by boat on rivers and then walk through the forest.
48623.m: You reach Angel Falls by boat and on foot.

48624.q: When does the most water plunge down at Angel Falls?
48624.e: In the rainy season it rains a great deal on top of the mountain. Then especially large amounts of water fall down.
48624.m: Angel Falls carry the most water in the rainy season.

48625.q: Who are Angel Falls named after?
48625.e: The waterfall is named after the pilot Jimmie Angel. He flew over it in the 1930s and made it famous.
48625.m: Angel Falls are named after the pilot Jimmie Angel.

48626.q: What kind of mountain do Angel Falls plunge down from?
48626.e: The waterfall plunges down from Auyán-tepui. This is a table mountain with a flat top and steep walls.
48626.m: Angel Falls drop from a table mountain.

48627.q: What happens to a lot of the water of Angel Falls on its long way down?
48627.e: The water falls so far that much of it breaks up into fine droplets. At the bottom it arrives like mist.
48627.m: At Angel Falls the water turns to mist.

48628.q: Roughly how much higher than the Staubbach Falls in Lauterbrunnen are Angel Falls?
a: About a hundred times as high
48628.e: The Staubbach Falls are just under 300 metres high, Angel Falls 979 metres. That is about three times as high.
48628.m: Angel Falls are about three times as high as the Staubbach Falls.

48629.q: What shape is the area where the Nile flows into the sea?
48629.e: Before the sea the Nile splits into several branches. From above the Nile Delta looks like a big triangle.
48629.m: The Nile Delta is shaped like a triangle.

48630.q: In which mountain range does the Amazon rise?
48630.e: The sources of the Amazon are high up in the Andes in Peru.
48630.m: The Amazon rises in the Andes.

48631.q: How do many people along the Mekong carry their goods from place to place?
48631.e: For many people the Mekong is like a road. They use boats to carry fruit, rice and other goods from village to village.
48631.m: Along the Mekong many things are transported by boat.

48632.q: Through what kind of landscape does most of the Congo flow?
48632.e: The Congo flows through the second largest rainforest on Earth. It rains a great deal there.
48632.m: The Congo flows through dense rainforest.

48633.q: What is special about the delta formed by the Ganges and the Brahmaputra together?
a: It is the largest river delta in the world
It is the smallest river delta in Asia
48633.e: Together the Ganges and the Brahmaputra form the largest river delta on Earth. It lies mainly in Bangladesh and opens into the Bay of Bengal.
48633.m: The Ganges and Brahmaputra form the largest delta in the world.

48634.q: What happens at Niagara Falls in the evening?
a: They are lit up in colours
48634.e: In the evening big spotlights light up the falls in many colours. This attracts lots of visitors.
48634.m: Niagara Falls glow in bright colours in the evening.

48635.q: Which is the largest lake in the world?
48635.e: The Caspian Sea has a larger area than any other lake on Earth. It is much bigger than the whole of Switzerland.
48635.m: The largest lake in the world is the Caspian Sea.

48636.q: Why does the Caspian Sea count as a lake and not a sea?
a: It is completely surrounded by land.
It is only a few metres deep.
It is in the middle of the Alps.
It is frozen all year round.
48636.e: A sea is connected to the ocean. The Caspian Sea has no connection to the ocean; it is surrounded by land on all sides.
48636.m: The Caspian Sea is a lake because it is surrounded by land.

48637.q: What does the water in the Caspian Sea taste like?
48637.e: The water in the Caspian Sea contains salt. But it is much less salty than ocean water.
48637.m: The Caspian Sea has slightly salty water.

48638.q: How many countries lie on the shore of the Caspian Sea?
48638.e: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, including Russia and Kazakhstan.
48638.m: Five countries share the shore of the Caspian Sea.

48639.q: Which country lies on the Caspian Sea?
48639.e: Iran lies on the southern shore of the Caspian Sea. Spain, Egypt and India are far away from it.
48639.m: Iran borders the Caspian Sea in the south.

48640.q: Between which two continents does the Caspian Sea lie?
48640.e: The Caspian Sea lies on the border between Europe and Asia. Part of its shores belongs to Europe, another part to Asia.
48640.m: The Caspian Sea lies between Europe and Asia.

48641.q: Which long river flows into the Caspian Sea?
48641.e: The Volga is the longest river in Europe. It flows through Russia and into the Caspian Sea.
48641.m: The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea.

48642.q: Which animal with flippers lives in the Caspian Sea?
48642.e: The Caspian seal lives in the Caspian Sea. It is found nowhere else in the world.
48642.m: The Caspian seal lives only in the Caspian Sea.

48643.q: From the eggs of which fish from the Caspian Sea is real caviar made?
48643.e: Real caviar is made from the eggs of the sturgeon. Several kinds of this large fish live in the Caspian Sea.
48643.m: Real caviar comes from the sturgeon.

48644.q: In which country is Lake Baikal?
48644.e: Lake Baikal is in the east of Russia. It is one of the best-known lakes in the country.

a: Long and narrow like a crescent
48645.e: Lake Baikal is over 600 kilometres long, but only up to about 80 kilometres wide. On the map it looks like a narrow crescent.
48645.m: Lake Baikal is long and narrow like a crescent.

48646.q: Roughly how deep is Lake Baikal at its deepest point?
48646.e: Lake Baikal is about 1640 metres deep at its deepest point. That is about as high as a medium-sized mountain in Switzerland.
48646.m: Lake Baikal is over 1600 metres deep.

48647.q: In which cold region is Lake Baikal?
48647.e: Siberia is a huge, cold region in Russia. That is where Lake Baikal is.

48648.q: What happens to Lake Baikal in winter?
48648.e: It is very cold there in winter. Lake Baikal then gets a thick layer of ice that you can walk on.
48648.m: Lake Baikal freezes over in winter.

48649.q: Which special animal lives in the fresh water of Lake Baikal?
48649.e: The Baikal seal lives in Lake Baikal. It is the only kind of seal that lives only in fresh water.
48649.m: The Baikal seal lives in the fresh water of Lake Baikal.

48650.q: What is the water of Lake Baikal known for?
a: It is as thick as honey.
48650.e: The water of Lake Baikal is especially clean and clear. Under water you can see up to 40 metres.
48650.m: Lake Baikal has very clear water.

48651.q: Roughly how old is Lake Baikal?
48651.e: Lake Baikal is about 25 million years old. It is considered the oldest lake in the world.
48651.m: Lake Baikal is the oldest lake in the world.

48652.q: How many rivers flow out of Lake Baikal?
48652.e: Over 300 rivers flow into Lake Baikal. Only one single river flows out, the Angara.
48652.m: Only the Angara flows out of Lake Baikal.

48653.q: Which lake is the largest lake in Africa?
48653.e: Lake Victoria has the largest area of all the lakes in Africa. It is about the size of Ireland.
48653.m: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa.

48654.q: Who is Lake Victoria named after?
48654.e: An English explorer named the lake after Queen Victoria. At that time she was Queen of Great Britain.
48654.m: Lake Victoria bears the name of a queen.

48655.q: Which famous river begins at Lake Victoria?
