49017.e: Horses are very important for the nomads in Mongolia. They ride them and use them to herd their animals.
49017.m: Horses are very important in Mongolia.

49018.q: What is the steppe in North America called?
49018.e: The steppe in North America is called the prairie. Huge herds of bison used to live there.
49018.m: The steppe in North America is called the prairie.

49019.q: What is the steppe in Argentina called?
49019.e: The steppe in Argentina is called the pampas. Today many cattle graze there.
49019.m: The steppe in Argentina is called the pampas.

49020.q: Which grain is grown on many steppe soils today?
49020.e: Steppe soils are often very fertile. That is why a lot of wheat is grown there.
49020.m: A lot of wheat grows on steppe soils.

49021.q: What kind of forest is the taiga?
49021.e: The taiga is a huge coniferous forest in the cold north of the Earth. It is the largest forest area in the world.
49021.m: The taiga is a huge coniferous forest.

49022.q: The taiga is a huge forest in the cold north. Which trees mainly grow there?
49022.e: In the taiga mainly conifers grow, such as spruces, pines and larches. They cope well with the cold.
49022.m: Mainly conifers grow in the taiga.

49023.q: In which country is most of the taiga?
49023.e: Russia is the largest country on Earth. A large part of it is covered with taiga.
49023.m: Most of the taiga is in Russia.

49024.q: Which country in North America also has a lot of taiga?
49024.e: Canada lies far to the north. Large parts of the country are covered with coniferous forest.
49024.m: Canada also has a lot of taiga.

49025.q: Which large animal with broad antlers lives in the huge coniferous forest of the cold north?
49025.e: The elk, called moose in North America, is the largest deer in the world. The males have broad, shovel-shaped antlers.
49025.m: The elk is the largest deer in the world.

49026.q: Which predator lives in the huge coniferous forest of the cold north?
49026.e: The brown bear lives in the coniferous forests of the north. In winter it rests in a den.
49026.m: The brown bear lives in the coniferous forest of the north.

49027.q: The taiga is a huge forest in the far north. What are the winters like there?
49027.e: Winter in the taiga lasts many months. It can freeze very hard there.
49027.m: In the taiga the winters are long and cold.

49028.q: Which landscape lies north of the taiga?
49028.e: Where it gets even colder, the forests of the taiga stop. Further north the treeless tundra begins.
49028.m: The tundra lies north of the taiga.

49029.q: Which conifer of the taiga loses its needles in autumn?
49029.e: The larch is a special conifer. In autumn its needles turn yellow and fall off, here in the Alps too.
49029.m: The larch sheds its needles in autumn.

49030.q: What is the area around the North Pole called?
49030.e: The area around the North Pole is called the Arctic. It is cold there all year round.
49030.m: The Arctic is in the very north of the Earth.

49031.q: What lies in the middle of the Arctic?
49031.e: In the middle of the Arctic there is no land, but a sea. It is often covered with ice.
49031.m: In the middle of the Arctic there is a frozen sea.

49032.q: Which large island lies in the Arctic?
49032.e: Greenland is the largest island in the world and lies largely in the Arctic. It is almost completely covered with ice.
49032.m: Greenland is a huge island full of ice in the far north.

49033.q: What is it called when the sun shines at night too in the Arctic summer?
49033.e: In summer the sun does not set in the Arctic for weeks. This is called the midnight sun.
49033.m: With the midnight sun it stays light at night too.

49034.q: What is the time in winter called when the sun does not rise at all in the Arctic?
49034.e: In winter the sun stays below the horizon in the Arctic for weeks. This dark time is called the polar night.
49034.m: In the polar night it stays dark during the day too.

49035.q: Which fox lives in the Arctic and has white fur in winter?
49035.e: The Arctic fox has white fur in winter. That way it is well camouflaged in the snow.
49035.m: The Arctic fox has white fur in winter.

49036.q: Which deer with big antlers live in the far north and pull Father Christmas’s sleigh in stories?
49036.e: Reindeer live in the cold regions of the north. With them, the females have antlers too.
49036.m: Reindeer live in the far north and have antlers.

49037.q: Which country has a part in the Arctic?
49037.e: The north of Norway lies in the Arctic. Russia, Canada, the USA with Alaska and Denmark with Greenland also have areas there.
49037.m: Norway reaches far up into the Arctic.

49038.q: About how thick is the sea ice at the North Pole?
49038.e: The sea ice in the Arctic is usually two to three metres thick. Where floes are pushed on top of each other, it can be thicker.
49038.m: The ice at the North Pole is only a few metres thick.

49039.q: What happens to the ice at the North Pole when the Earth gets warmer?
49039.e: Because the Earth is getting warmer, more ice melts in the Arctic in summer. The sea ice becomes smaller and thinner.
49039.m: When it gets warmer, the ice at the North Pole melts.

49040.q: Why can a polar bear walk about in the middle of the sea at the North Pole?
a: Because the sea is very shallow there
Because there are lots of stones there
Because there is lots of sand there
49040.e: At the North Pole it is so cold that the sea water freezes. Polar bears can walk on this sea ice and hunt seals.
49040.m: At the North Pole the sea is frozen into ice.

49041.q: When is there the most ice at the North Pole?
49041.e: In the cold, dark winter the sea freezes and the ice grows. In summer part of it melts.
49041.m: In winter the ice at the North Pole grows.

49042.q: You are standing exactly on the North Pole. In which direction does every step take you?
49042.e: From the North Pole you cannot go any further north in any direction. That is why every path from there leads south.
49042.m: At the North Pole every path leads south.

49043.q: What is the sea called that the ice at the North Pole floats on?
49043.e: The ice at the North Pole floats on the Arctic Ocean. It is also called the Northern Polar Sea.
49043.m: The ice at the North Pole floats on the Arctic Ocean.

49044.q: What is the most northerly point on Earth called?
49044.e: The North Pole is the most northerly point on Earth. You cannot go any further north.
49044.m: The North Pole is the point at the very top of the Earth.

49045.e: The Amundsen-Scott Station stands almost exactly at the South Pole. Scientists live and work there.
49045.m: The Amundsen-Scott Station is at the South Pole.

49046.q: Which country runs the research station at the South Pole?
49046.e: The Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station is run by the USA. It has existed since the 1950s.
49046.m: The station at the South Pole belongs to the USA.

49047.q: Who was the first person at the South Pole?
49047.e: Roald Amundsen was the first to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911. Robert Scott arrived about a month later. The station at the South Pole is named after both.
49047.m: Roald Amundsen was the first to reach the South Pole.

49048.q: What do the people at the station at the South Pole do?
49048.e: Scientists live at the station. They study, for example, the ice, the weather and the sky.
49048.m: Research is done at the South Pole station.

49049.q: How do scientists usually get to the station at the South Pole?
49049.e: The journey across the ice to the South Pole is very long and difficult. That is why most people fly in planes that have skis and land on the snow.
49049.m: You fly to the South Pole in planes that land on snow.

49050.q: About how long does the sun shine without a break at the South Pole?
49050.e: At the South Pole the sun shines without a break for about half a year. After that it is dark for about half a year.
49050.m: At the South Pole it is light for half a year and dark for half a year.

49051.q: What does the research station at the South Pole stand on?
49051.e: The station stands on the ice of Antarctica, about 2,800 metres above sea level. The ice underneath is very thick.
49051.m: The station at the South Pole stands on a thick layer of ice.

49052.q: Roughly how much of an iceberg is under water?
49052.e: About nine tenths of an iceberg lie under water. You only see the tip.
49052.m: Most of an iceberg is hidden under water.

49053.q: Which famous ship sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
49053.e: The Titanic hit an iceberg on the night of 14 to 15 April 1912 and sank a few hours later. Many people died.
49053.m: The Titanic sank after hitting an iceberg.

49054.q: What kind of water is an iceberg made of?
49054.e: Icebergs come from glacier ice. This ice comes from snow, so it is not salty.
49054.m: Icebergs are made of fresh water.

49055.q: Why does an iceberg float in the sea?
49055.e: Ice is lighter than the same amount of liquid water. That is why it floats on top.
49055.m: Ice floats because it is lighter than water.

49056.q: What is it called when a glacier by the sea lets an iceberg break off?
49056.e: When a piece of the glacier breaks off into the sea, people say: the glacier is calving.
49056.m: A glacier calves when an iceberg breaks off.

49057.q: What are the flat, wide icebergs in Antarctica called?
49057.e: In Antarctica flat icebergs often break off the ice shelf. They look like a table and are called tabular icebergs.
49057.m: Tabular icebergs are flat like a table.

49058.q: What happens to an iceberg that drifts into warm sea?
49058.e: In warmer water the iceberg slowly melts. In the end only water is left.
49058.m: In the warm sea an iceberg melts.

49059.q: What does a polar bear often use to find its prey from far away?
49059.e: Polar bears have a very good sense of smell. They can smell seals even under the snow.
49059.m: The polar bear has a very good nose.

49060.q: What do polar bears like to eat most?
49060.e: Polar bears mainly hunt seals on the sea ice. The fatty meat gives them lots of energy.
49060.m: Polar bears like hunting seals best.

49061.q: What colour is a polar bear’s skin?
49061.e: Under its pale fur the polar bear has black skin. Dark skin takes in the sun’s warmth well.
49061.m: A polar bear has black skin under its pale fur.

49062.q: Why is the polar bear well protected from the cold?
a: It always stays in the water
49062.e: The polar bear has thick fur and a thick layer of fat. Both keep it warm.
49062.m: Fur and fat keep the polar bear warm.

49063.q: Where does a polar bear mother give birth to her cubs?
49063.e: In winter the female polar bear digs a den in the snow. The cubs are born there.
49063.m: Polar bear cubs are born in a snow den.

49064.q: Can a polar bear swim well?
49064.e: Polar bears are very good swimmers. They can swim long distances from ice floe to ice floe.

49065.q: Why do polar bears have a hard time when the sea ice melts?
49065.e: Polar bears catch seals from the ice. Without sea ice it is harder for them to find food.
49065.m: Polar bears need the sea ice for hunting.

49066.q: How many cubs does a female polar bear usually have at once?
49066.e: A female polar bear usually has two cubs, sometimes only one. They stay with their mother for more than two years.
49066.m: Female polar bears usually have twins.

49067.e: The emperor penguin is the largest kind of penguin. It grows more than a metre tall.
49067.m: The emperor penguin is the largest penguin.

49068.q: Where does the emperor penguin live?
49068.e: Emperor penguins live only around Antarctica. There are no penguins at the North Pole.
49068.m: Emperor penguins live in the south, in Antarctica.

49069.q: In emperor penguins, who keeps the egg warm?
49069.e: In emperor penguins the father incubates the egg. During this time the mother goes to feed in the sea.
49069.m: In emperor penguins the father keeps the egg warm.

49070.q: Where does an emperor penguin carry its egg while incubating it?
49070.e: The egg rests on the penguin’s feet. A warm fold of skin on its belly covers it.
49070.m: The emperor penguin keeps the egg warm on its feet.

49071.q: What do emperor penguins do when an icy storm comes?
49071.e: Many emperor penguins stand close together and keep each other warm. They keep swapping from the edge to the warm middle.
49071.m: Emperor penguins keep warm by huddling together.

49072.e: Penguins are birds that cannot fly. But they swim very well with their wings.
49072.m: Penguins do not fly; they swim with their wings.

49073.e: Emperor penguins dive in the sea for fish, squid and small crustaceans.
49073.m: Emperor penguins get their food from the sea.

49074.q: What colour is an emperor penguin on its neck?
49074.e: The emperor penguin is black and white. On its neck and ears it has yellow-orange patches.
49074.m: The emperor penguin has yellow patches on its neck.

49075.q: In which season do emperor penguins breed?
49075.e: Emperor penguins breed in the middle of the freezing winter, when it is almost always dark. So the egg has to be kept very warm.
49075.m: Emperor penguins breed in the cold winter.

49076.q: What do seals have instead of legs?
49076.e: Seals have flippers. With them they swim very well in the water.

49077.q: What protects seals from the cold in icy water?
49077.e: Seals have a thick layer of blubber under their skin. It keeps them warm.
49077.m: Blubber keeps seals warm in cold water.

49078.e: The elephant seal is the largest seal. The males have a nose that looks like a short trunk.
49078.m: The elephant seal is the largest seal.

49079.q: Which seal of Antarctica also eats penguins?
49079.e: The leopard seal is a strong hunter in the Southern Ocean. It eats fish, penguins and even other seals.

49080.q: Why do seals make holes in the ice?
49080.e: Seals are mammals and must breathe air. Under the ice they need breathing holes.
49080.m: Seals need air and breathe through holes in the ice.

49081.e: Seals dive in the sea and mainly catch fish. Some also eat squid or crustaceans.

49082.q: Which seals have small ear flaps and can walk on their flippers on land?
49082.e: Sea lions have small ears and can turn their back flippers forwards. That way they walk quite skilfully on land.
49082.m: Sea lions have small ears and walk on their flippers.

49083.q: Which animal group do seals belong to?
49083.e: Seals are mammals. The young drink milk from their mother.

49084.q: What does a walrus have in its mouth that you can see clearly?
49084.e: The walrus has two long tusks. They are extra-long canine teeth.
49084.m: The walrus has two long tusks.

49285.q: What are the two seasons in the savannah called?
49285.e: The savannah has a rainy season and a dry season. Instead of cold and warm, it changes between wet and dry.
49285.m: In the savannah, the rainy season and the dry season take turns.

49286.q: How does an elephant drink at the waterhole?
a: It sucks water into its trunk
49286.e: The elephant sucks water into its trunk. Then it squirts it into its mouth.
49286.m: Elephants drink with the help of their trunk.

49287.q: How can elephants find water in the dry season?
a: They dig in the dry riverbed
49287.e: Elephants dig in the dried-up riverbed with their feet, trunk and tusks. That way they reach water in the ground.

49288.q: Why do zebras and wildebeest like to drink at the waterhole in large groups?
a: They want to learn to swim
49288.e: When drinking, the animals lower their heads and are not paying attention. In a group, there is always one animal that notices when a predator comes.
49288.m: Animals at the waterhole are safer in a group.

49289.q: Why do some animals wallow in the mud at the waterhole?
49289.e: Mud cools the skin and protects it from the hot sun. That is why warthogs and buffalo like to wallow.
49289.m: A mud bath cools you down in the heat.

49290.q: In which landscape can the cheetah hunt best?
49290.e: The cheetah needs a clear view and lots of space for its fast sprint. That is why it prefers to hunt in open grassland.
49290.m: The cheetah prefers to hunt in open grassland.

49291.q: About how fast can a cheetah run?
49291.e: For a short time a cheetah reaches about 100 kilometres per hour. That makes it the fastest land animal in the world.
49291.m: A cheetah runs about as fast as a car on the motorway.

49292.q: How long can a cheetah run that fast?
49292.e: The cheetah is a sprinter. After a few hundred metres it is exhausted and has to rest.
49292.m: The cheetah runs fast, but only for a short time.

49293.q: What does a cheetah have on its face?
49293.e: A cheetah has black stripes running from its eyes to its mouth. They look like tear tracks.

49294.q: When does the cheetah usually hunt?
a: In the middle of the night
49294.e: Cheetahs usually hunt during the day, often in the morning or late afternoon. At night lions and hyenas are out and about.
49294.m: The cheetah hunts during the day.

49295.q: What prey does a cheetah often hunt?
49295.e: Cheetahs mainly hunt medium-sized, fast animals such as gazelles and impalas.

49296.q: What pattern does a cheetah's fur have?
49296.e: The cheetah has yellowish fur with lots of small, solid black spots.

49297.q: What helps the cheetah not to fall over when running round bends?
49297.e: The cheetah uses its long tail like a rudder. It helps it keep its balance on fast turns.
49297.m: The tail helps the cheetah steer.

49298.q: In which country is the Okavango Delta?
49298.e: The Okavango Delta is in the north of Botswana in southern Africa.
49298.m: The Okavango Delta is in Botswana.

49299.q: What is special about the Okavango River?
a: It does not flow into the sea
49299.e: The Okavango does not flow into the sea. Its water spreads out in the delta, seeps away and evaporates.
49299.m: The Okavango never reaches the sea.

49300.q: Which desert borders the Okavango Delta?
49300.e: The Okavango Delta lies in the middle of the Kalahari region. The plentiful water in the dry area attracts animals.
49300.m: The Okavango Delta is a water oasis in the Kalahari.

49301.q: Which boat do people in the Okavango Delta often use?
49301.e: In the delta people travel in narrow dugout canoes called mokoro. They are pushed along with a long pole.
49301.m: In the Okavango Delta people travel by dugout canoe.

49302.q: What does the Okavango Delta look like?
49302.e: In the delta the river splits into many small channels. Between them are islands, swamps and grassland.
49302.m: The Okavango Delta is made up of many channels and islands.

49303.q: What is special about the Okavango River in Africa?
49303.e: The Okavango flows into the Kalahari and branches out there into a huge inland delta. There its water seeps away and evaporates. Since 2014 the delta has been a World Heritage Site.
49303.m: The Okavango ends in a delta in the middle of the land.

49304.q: Which large animals live in especially large numbers in the Okavango Delta area?
49304.e: A great many elephants live in the north of Botswana. They like to come to the water in the delta.
49304.m: Lots of elephants live in the Okavango Delta.

49305.q: When does the Okavango Delta have the most water?
49305.e: The rainwater from Angola takes months to reach the delta. That is why the delta is fullest in, of all times, the dry season.
49305.m: The Okavango Delta is fullest in the dry season.

49306.q: Where does a hippo usually spend the hot day?
49306.e: Hippos lie in the water during the day. That keeps their sensitive skin moist and cool.
49306.m: Hippos spend the day in the water.

49307.e: Hippos are plant-eaters. They mainly eat grass, and lots of it.

49308.q: When does the hippo go on land to feed?
49308.e: At night hippos leave the water. They often walk for kilometres to eat grass.
49308.m: Hippos feed on land at night.

49309.q: What other name does the hippo have?
49309.e: The hippo's full name is hippopotamus. It lives in the rivers and lakes of Africa.
49309.m: The hippo is also called the hippopotamus.

49310.q: What protects the hippo's skin from the sun?
49310.e: Hippos produce a reddish liquid on their skin. It works like sun cream.
49310.m: Hippos have their own sun protection.

49311.q: How does a hippo often move about underwater?
49311.e: Hippos are heavy and hardly swim properly. They walk or bounce along the bottom underwater.
49311.m: Hippos walk along the bottom underwater.

49312.q: What can you often only see when a hippo is lying in the water?
49312.e: The eyes, ears and nostrils are on top of the head. So the hippo can go almost completely underwater and still breathe and look around.
49312.m: With a hippo, only the eyes, ears and nose stick out of the water.

49313.q: Is the hippo a harmless animal?
49313.e: Hippos defend their territory fiercely and can attack very quickly. They are among the most dangerous animals in Africa.

49314.q: Which animals are the hippo's closest relatives?
49314.e: Although its name means “river horse”, the hippo is not related to the horse. Its closest living relatives are whales.
49314.m: The hippo is related to whales.

49315.q: What does a hippo show when it opens its mouth wide?
49315.e: A hippo opens its mouth very wide and shows its long canine teeth. That is how it threatens other animals.
49315.m: With its mouth open wide, the hippo is making a threat.

49316.q: What sounds does a cheetah make?
49316.e: The cheetah cannot roar. It purrs like a pet cat and makes chirping sounds, almost like a bird.
49316.m: The cheetah purrs, but it does not roar.

49317.q: About how tall is a baby giraffe at birth?
49317.e: A newborn giraffe is about 1.8 metres tall and weighs around 50 kilograms. So it is taller than most adults.
49317.m: Even a baby giraffe is very tall.

49318.q: About how thick is a rhino's skin?
49318.e: A rhino's skin is very thick, in some places up to about 5 centimetres. It works like armour.

49319.q: About how many individual reefs make up the Great Barrier Reef?
49319.e: The Great Barrier Reef is not one single reef. It is made up of about 2,900 individual reefs and many small islands.
49319.m: The Great Barrier Reef is made up of thousands of reefs.

49320.q: Which large whales come to the Great Barrier Reef every year to have their young?
49320.e: In winter humpback whales swim from the cold seas in the south to the warm reef. There they give birth to their young.
49320.m: Humpback whales have their young in the warm water near the reef.

49321.q: Which sea cow eats seagrass near the Great Barrier Reef?
49321.e: The dugong is a sea cow. It eats seagrass in the meadows in the shallow water near the reef.
49321.m: The dugong is a sea cow that eats seagrass.

49322.q: About how long is the Great Barrier Reef?
49322.e: The reef stretches for about 2,300 kilometres along the coast. That is much longer than the whole of Switzerland.
49322.m: The Great Barrier Reef is over 2,000 kilometres long.

49323.q: How big is the area of the Great Barrier Reef compared with Switzerland?
49323.e: The reef area covers about 344,000 square kilometres. Switzerland has about 41,000 square kilometres.
49323.m: The Great Barrier Reef is much bigger than Switzerland.

49324.q: Which famous list has the Great Barrier Reef been on since 1981?
a: List of the Wonders of the World
49324.e: In 1981 the Great Barrier Reef was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List as a natural site.
49324.m: The Great Barrier Reef is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

49325.q: What harms the corals of the Great Barrier Reef most?
49325.e: If the seawater gets too warm, the corals become ill and can die. That has already happened many times on the Great Barrier Reef.
49325.m: Water that is too warm harms the corals of the reef.

49326.q: Which animal eats lots of corals on the Great Barrier Reef?
49326.e: The crown-of-thorns starfish has lots of spines and eats corals. When there are very many of them, they badly damage the reef.

49328.q: Which city is a well-known starting point for trips to the Great Barrier Reef?
49328.e: Cairns is in the north-east of Australia, right by the sea. Many boats go to the reef from there.
49328.m: Many boats go to the Great Barrier Reef from Cairns.

49329.e: Corals look like plants or stones. In fact they are small animals.

49330.q: In what kind of water do most coral reefs grow?
49330.e: Reef-building corals need warm seawater. That is why most reefs are in the tropics.
49330.m: Coral reefs grow in warm seas.

49331.q: What do corals build their hard skeleton from?
49331.e: Corals make limestone. Over time, many limestone skeletons together form a whole reef.
49331.m: Corals build their skeleton from limestone.

49332.q: What is it called when corals lose their colour and turn white?
49332.e: In coral bleaching, corals lose their colour. Then you can see their white skeleton.
49332.m: In coral bleaching, corals turn white.

49333.q: Which colourful fish nibbles at corals and makes fine white sand as it does so?
49333.e: The parrotfish has a mouth like a beak. It nibbles algae off the corals and passes out ground-up limestone as fine sand.
49333.m: Parrotfish make fine white sand on the reef.

49334.q: Why do coral reefs only grow where the sea is not deep?
a: They need sand from the beach
49334.e: Corals need lots of light to live. In deep water it is too dark.
49334.m: Reef corals need lots of sunlight.

49335.q: What is a ring-shaped coral reef with a lagoon in the middle called?
49335.e: An atoll is a ring of coral reefs and small islands. In the middle there is a lagoon.
49335.m: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef.

49336.q: What are coral reefs often called because so many kinds of animals live there?
49336.e: A huge variety of animals live in coral reefs. That is why they are compared with rainforests.
49336.m: Coral reefs are the rainforests of the sea.

49337.q: What is a single small coral animal called?
49337.e: A coral animal is called a polyp. Many polyps live together in a colony.
49337.m: A single coral animal is called a polyp.

49338.q: How long can a blue whale grow?
49338.e: Large blue whales grow to about 30 metres long. That is about as long as two buses one behind the other.
49338.m: A blue whale can grow to about 30 metres long.

49339.q: How heavy can a blue whale get?
49339.e: A large blue whale weighs well over 100 tonnes. That is as heavy as many elephants put together.
49339.m: A blue whale weighs over 100 tonnes.

49340.q: What does the blue whale mainly eat?
49340.e: The blue whale mainly eats krill. These are small crustaceans that live in huge swarms.
49340.m: The blue whale mainly eats small crustaceans called krill.

49341.q: Which group of animals does the blue whale belong to?
49341.e: Whales are mammals. They breathe air with lungs and feed their young on milk.
49341.m: The blue whale is a mammal, not a fish.

49342.q: What can you see when a blue whale breathes out at the surface?
a: Lots of air bubbles in the sand
49342.e: When breathing out, the blue whale blows warm, moist air upwards. This column is called a “blow” and can be about 9 metres high.
49342.m: When a whale breathes out, you see a tall column.

49343.q: What does the blue whale have in its mouth instead of teeth?
49343.e: Baleen is made of long plates of horn-like material. The whale uses it to sieve its food out of the water.
49343.m: The blue whale has baleen instead of teeth.

49344.q: About how long is a baby blue whale at birth?
49344.e: A newborn blue whale is already about 7 metres long. It weighs about as much as two cars.
49344.m: Even a baby blue whale is about 7 metres long.

49345.q: Why are there only a few blue whales left today?
a: They were heavily hunted in the past
49345.e: In the past a great many blue whales were hunted. Today they are protected, but there are still only a few.
49345.m: Blue whales are protected today because they were almost wiped out.

49346.q: What does a dolphin breathe through?
49346.e: Dolphins breathe air. To do so they come to the surface and breathe through the blowhole on top of their head.
49346.m: Dolphins breathe through the blowhole on their head.

49347.q: How do dolphins find their prey in murky water?
49347.e: Dolphins send out clicking sounds. The echo tells them where a fish is swimming.
49347.m: Dolphins locate prey with clicks and echoes.

a: With one half of the brain
49348.e: When they sleep, dolphins keep one half of the brain awake. That way they can keep breathing and watch out for danger.
49348.m: Dolphins always sleep with only one half of the brain.

49349.e: Dolphins usually live in groups. They hunt and play together.
49349.m: Dolphins like to live in groups.

49350.q: Which large sea mammal belongs to the dolphin family?
49350.e: The orca, also called the killer whale, is the largest dolphin. It is black and white.
49350.m: The orca is the largest dolphin.

49351.q: What is the best-known kind of dolphin called?
49351.e: The bottlenose dolphin is the best-known dolphin. It is grey and lives in many seas. The harbour porpoise, narwhal and beluga are other toothed whales.
49351.m: The bottlenose dolphin is the best-known dolphin.

49352.q: How do dolphins call each other?
49352.e: Every dolphin has its own whistle. It works almost like a name.
49352.m: Dolphins call each other with their own whistles.

49353.q: How does a dolphin move its tail fin when swimming?
49353.e: A dolphin's tail fin is horizontal. It beats it up and down, whereas a fish moves its tail from side to side.
49353.m: Dolphins beat their tail fin up and down.

49354.q: Apart from the sea, where else do dolphins live?
49354.e: There are river dolphins, for example in the Amazon in South America.

49355.q: Which fish is the largest fish in the world?
49355.e: The whale shark is the largest fish. It can grow to over 12 metres long.
49355.m: The whale shark is the largest fish in the world.

49356.q: What does the whale shark mainly eat?
49356.e: The whale shark filters tiny living things, called plankton, out of the water. It is harmless to people.
49356.m: The whale shark eats tiny plankton.

49357.q: What is a shark's skeleton made of?
49357.e: Sharks do not have a skeleton of bone, but one of cartilage. You have cartilage in your ears too.
49357.m: Sharks have a skeleton made of cartilage.

49358.q: How did the hammerhead shark get its name?
a: From the shape of its head
49358.e: The hammerhead shark's head is wide like a hammer. Its eyes are at the ends.
49358.m: The hammerhead shark has a head like a hammer.

49359.q: What is a shark especially good at?
a: Staying on land for a long time
49359.e: Sharks have a very good sense of smell. They notice even the tiniest traces in the water.
49359.m: Sharks have a very keen nose.

49360.q: How often do sharks attack people?
a: Every time someone swims in the sea
49360.e: Shark attacks on people are very rare. Sharks are caught by people far more often.
49360.m: Sharks only very rarely attack people.

49361.q: Since when have there been sharks on Earth?
49361.e: Sharks have existed for over 400 million years. The first dinosaurs lived much later.
49361.m: There were sharks even before the dinosaurs.

49362.q: What do sea turtles breathe with?
49362.e: Sea turtles are reptiles and breathe with lungs. They have to come to the surface to breathe.
49362.m: Sea turtles come up to the surface for air.

49363.q: How many species of sea turtle are there?
49363.e: There are seven species of sea turtle. Almost all of them are endangered.
49363.m: There are seven species of sea turtle.

49364.q: What decides whether a female or a male hatches from a sea turtle egg?
49364.e: If the sand is warmer, more females hatch. If it is cooler, more males hatch.
49364.m: The warmth of the sand decides whether a female hatches.

49365.q: Why do sea turtles sometimes eat plastic bags?
a: They use them to clean the sea
They build a nest with them
49365.e: A plastic bag in the water looks like a jellyfish. The plastic can make the turtle ill.
49365.m: Plastic in the sea is dangerous for turtles.

49366.q: What is the largest sea turtle called?
49366.e: The leatherback turtle grows to about 2 metres long. Its shell is covered with leathery skin.
49366.m: The leatherback is the largest sea turtle.

49367.q: What can a sea turtle not do that many tortoises can?
49367.e: Sea turtles cannot pull their head and legs into their shell. But they are nimble swimmers.
49367.m: Sea turtles cannot pull in their head.

49368.q: What do sea turtles have instead of feet with toes?
49368.e: Their legs have become wide flippers. With them they can swim well.

49369.q: Where do newly hatched sea turtles crawl to?
49369.e: The little turtles dig their way out of the sand. Then they hurry to the sea as fast as they can.
49369.m: Young sea turtles crawl straight to the sea.

49370.q: Where do female sea turtles often return to lay their eggs?
a: To the beach where they were born
49370.e: Many females swim thousands of kilometres back. They often lay their eggs on the beach where they hatched themselves.
49370.m: Sea turtles find their way back to the beach where they were born.

49371.q: Which animal does the clownfish live in?
49371.e: The clownfish lives between the tentacles of a sea anemone. There it is safe from enemies.
49371.m: The clownfish lives in a sea anemone.

49372.q: Why does the clownfish not get stung by the tentacles of the animal it lives in?
a: A layer of slime protects it
49372.e: The clownfish has a special layer of slime on its skin. That is why the tentacles do not sting it.
49372.m: A layer of slime protects the clownfish.

49373.q: What colours is the well-known clownfish?
49373.e: The best-known clownfish is orange with white stripes. The stripes often have a black edge.
49373.m: The clownfish is orange with white stripes.

49374.q: In which animated film is a clownfish the main character?
49374.e: In the film “Finding Nemo”, a clownfish dad searches the sea for his son Nemo.

49375.q: What happens with clownfish when the female of a group dies?
a: The largest male becomes a female
The young grow up at once
49375.e: Clownfish can change from male to female. The largest male then becomes the new female.
49375.m: Clownfish can change from male to female.

49376.q: Where do clownfish live in the wild?
a: In cold seas near the ice
49376.e: Clownfish live in warm coral reefs in the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.

49377.q: About how big does a clownfish grow?
49377.e: Clownfish are small fish. Most grow to about 10 centimetres long.
49377.m: A clownfish is about as long as a finger.

49378.q: How does the clownfish help the animal it lives in?
a: It keeps it warm in winter
49378.e: The clownfish chases away fish that want to eat its host. Both animals help each other.
49378.m: The clownfish and its host help each other.

49379.q: Who mainly guards the eggs in clownfish?
49379.e: With clownfish it is mainly the father who looks after the eggs. He fans fresh water over them.
49379.m: With clownfish, the father guards the eggs.

49380.q: Why is it dark in the deep sea?
a: Sunlight does not reach that deep
The fish switch off the light
49380.e: Sunlight only gets a few hundred metres down into the sea. Below that it is pitch dark.
49380.m: The deep sea is dark because no sunlight gets there.

49381.q: What can many animals in the deep sea make themselves?
49381.e: Many deep-sea animals can glow. That is how they lure prey or find a partner.
49381.m: Many deep-sea animals can glow on their own.

49382.q: Which deep-sea fish lures prey with a glowing fishing rod on its head?
49382.e: The anglerfish has a kind of fishing rod with a glowing bait on its head. When a fish comes closer, it snaps it up.
49382.m: The anglerfish fishes with a glowing bait.

49383.q: How cold is the water in the deep sea usually?
a: Only a few degrees above zero
49383.e: The sun only warms the water at the top. Almost everywhere in the deep sea it is only a few degrees.
49383.m: The water in the deep sea is very cold.

49384.q: What drifts slowly down in the deep sea and is food for many animals?
49384.e: Marine snow is made of tiny remains of dead animals and plants. They sink slowly and look like snowflakes.
49384.m: Many deep-sea animals live on marine snow.

49385.q: What presses very hard on everything in the deep sea?
49385.e: There is a huge amount of water above the deep sea. Its weight presses on everything with great force.
49385.m: The water pressure in the deep sea is enormous.

49386.q: Which animal with long tentacles lives in the deep sea?
49386.e: The giant squid is a kind of cephalopod. With its tentacles it can be about 10 metres long, and it has huge eyes.
49386.m: The giant squid lives in the deep sea.

49387.q: Which whale dives especially deep to hunt squid?
49387.e: The sperm whale can dive over 1,000 metres deep. There it hunts squid.
49387.m: The sperm whale is a record-breaking diver.

49388.q: What is there in some places on the floor of the deep sea?
49388.e: In some places hot water streams out of the seabed. They are also called “black smokers”. Special animals such as tube worms live there.
49388.m: There are hot springs on the deep-sea floor.

49389.q: What is a jellyfish mostly made of?
49389.e: A jellyfish is about 98 per cent water. That is why it is so see-through and soft.
49389.m: Jellyfish are made almost entirely of water.

49390.q: What does a jellyfish not have?
49390.e: Jellyfish have no brain. They only have a simple network of nerves.

49391.q: What do jellyfish catch their prey with?
49391.e: The tentacles have stinging cells with venom. Jellyfish use them to paralyse small animals.
49391.m: Jellyfish catch prey with their stings.

49392.e: The jellyfish squeezes its bell together, pushing water out. That moves it forward.
49392.m: Jellyfish swim by squeezing their bell together.

49393.q: Which jellyfish can turn back into a young form?
49393.e: When in danger, the immortal jellyfish can turn back into a young polyp. Then it grows up all over again.
49393.m: The immortal jellyfish can become young again.

49394.q: The moon jellyfish also lives in the North Sea. What does it look like?
a: See-through with four rings in the middle
49394.e: The moon jellyfish has four ring-shaped patterns in the middle. It is also common in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea.
49394.m: The moon jellyfish has four rings in the middle.

49395.q: Which jellyfish is one of the largest jellyfish in the world?
49395.e: The lion's mane jellyfish often has a bell about a metre wide, in rare cases over 2 metres. Its tentacles are very long.
49395.m: The lion's mane jellyfish is a giant jellyfish.

49396.q: Which jellyfish is thought to be one of the most venomous animals in the sea?
49396.e: The box jellyfish, also called the sea wasp, lives mainly off Australia. Its venom is very strong and dangerous to people.
49396.m: The box jellyfish is a very venomous jellyfish.

49397.q: Are there jellyfish in Swiss lakes too?
49397.e: A small freshwater jellyfish lives in some Swiss lakes. It is only about 2 centimetres big, harmless to people and appears mainly in summer.
49397.m: There are small jellyfish in Swiss lakes too.

49398.e: Mangroves are trees and shrubs. They grow on tropical coasts right by the sea.
49398.m: Mangroves are trees by the sea.

49399.q: What do the roots of many mangroves look like?
49399.e: Many mangroves stand on stilt roots. That way they hold on in the soft mud.

49400.q: What kind of water can mangroves cope with?
49400.e: Most trees die in salt water. But mangroves can cope well with the salt.

49401.q: Why are mangroves important for many young fish?
a: As a feeding place for whales
As a sleeping place for birds
49401.e: Young fish can hide well between the roots. Large predators find it hard to get in there.
49401.m: Mangroves are a nursery for fish.

49402.q: How do mangroves protect the coast?
a: They slow down waves and storm surges
49402.e: The dense roots slow down the waves. That way the coast is damaged less during storms.
49402.m: Mangroves protect the coast from waves.

a: Where the tide comes in and goes out
In the middle of the desert
49403.e: Mangroves grow at the edge of the sea. At high tide they stand in water, at low tide in mud.
49403.m: Mangroves grow where the tide comes and goes.

49404.q: Which large predator lives in the mangrove forests of the Sundarbans in Asia?
49404.e: The Sundarbans in Bangladesh and India are a huge mangrove forest. The Bengal tiger, also called the royal Bengal tiger, lives there.
49404.m: Tigers live in the mangroves of the Sundarbans.

49405.q: The mudskipper is a fish from the mangroves. What can it do?
a: Blow itself up like a ball
Spend the winter under the ice
49405.e: The mudskipper can stay on land for a while. It hops across the mud with its front fins.
49405.m: The mudskipper hops across the mud.

49406.q: What is special about the seeds of some mangroves?
a: They sprout while still on the tree
49406.e: In some mangroves the seeds already sprout on the tree. Then the young plants drop off and carry on growing in the mud.
49406.m: Some mangrove seeds sprout while still on the tree.

49407.q: How many arms do most starfish have?
49407.e: Most starfish have five arms. But there are also kinds with many more arms.

49408.q: Where are a starfish's simple eyes?
a: At the tips of its arms
49408.e: There is a simple eye at the tip of each arm. With it the starfish can tell light from dark.
49408.m: Starfish see with the tips of their arms.

49409.q: How does a starfish eat a mussel?
a: It pushes its stomach out of its body
It cracks it open with its teeth
It sucks it up with a trunk
49409.e: The starfish pulls the mussel's shell open a crack. Then it pushes its stomach inside and digests it.
49409.m: The starfish digests its prey with its stomach outside its body.

49410.e: On the underside of its arms the starfish has many tiny tube feet with suckers. It crawls slowly with them.

49411.q: Which group of animals do starfish belong to?
49411.e: Starfish are not fish. They belong to the echinoderms, which means “spiny skins”, because their skin often has small spines.

49412.q: Which animal is a close relative of the starfish?
49412.e: The sea urchin is related to the starfish. Both have a body divided into five equal parts.
49412.m: Sea urchins and starfish are relatives.

a: At the tip of an arm
49413.e: A starfish's mouth is on its underside, right in the middle.
49413.m: The starfish has its mouth on its underside.

49414.e: Starfish need salt water. That is why they only live in the sea and never in lakes or rivers.
49414.m: Starfish only live in the salty sea.

49415.q: Which sea borders Egypt to the north?
49415.e: Egypt's north coast is on the Mediterranean. The city of Alexandria is there too.
49415.m: The Mediterranean lies to the north of Egypt.

49416.q: Which sea lies to the east of Egypt?
49416.e: In the east Egypt has a long coast on the Red Sea. There are colourful coral reefs there.
49416.m: The Red Sea lies to the east of Egypt.

49417.q: Which desert does most of Egypt belong to?
49417.e: Egypt is mostly desert. It is part of the Sahara, the largest hot desert in the world.
49417.m: Most of Egypt is desert and belongs to the Sahara.

49418.q: About how many people live in Egypt (as of 2024)?
49418.e: Over 100 million people live in Egypt. That is more than ten times as many as in Switzerland.
49418.m: Over 100 million people live in Egypt.

49419.q: Which famous canal for ships is in Egypt?
49419.e: The Suez Canal opened in 1869. Thanks to it, ships travelling between Europe and Asia no longer have to sail all the way round Africa.
49419.m: The Suez Canal in Egypt is an important shortcut for ships.

49420.q: Which animal was sacred in ancient Egypt and was even buried as a mummy?
49420.e: Cats were greatly honoured in ancient Egypt. Many cat mummies have been found.
49420.m: In ancient Egypt cats were sacred animals.

49421.q: Which young pharaoh became famous because of his tomb with a golden mask?
49421.e: Tutankhamun's tomb was discovered in 1922 in the Valley of the Kings. Inside was a magnificent death mask made of gold.
49421.m: Tutankhamun is famous for his golden death mask.

49422.q: What is the capital of Morocco?
49422.e: The capital of Morocco is Rabat. The king lives there and the government works there.
49422.m: Rabat is the capital of Morocco.

49423.q: Which city is the largest city in Morocco?
49423.e: Casablanca is the largest city in Morocco. It has a big port on the Atlantic.
49423.m: Casablanca is the largest city in Morocco.

49424.q: The old town of Chefchaouen in Morocco is famous for its colour. What colour are many of the houses there?
49424.e: In Chefchaouen many houses and alleys are painted light blue. That is why it is also called “the blue city”.
49424.m: Chefchaouen in Morocco is the blue city.

49425.q: Which strait separates Morocco from Spain?
49425.e: The Strait of Gibraltar lies between Morocco and Spain. At its narrowest point it is only about 14 kilometres wide.
49425.m: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Africa from Europe.

49426.q: Who is the head of state in Morocco?
49426.e: Morocco is a kingdom. A king is at the head of the state.
49426.m: Morocco is a kingdom with a king.

49427.q: Which city in Morocco is called “the Red City”?
49427.e: Many houses and walls in Marrakesh are built of reddish clay. That is why it is called “the Red City”.
49427.m: Marrakesh is called “the Red City” because of its reddish walls.

49428.q: Which ocean lies along the west coast of Morocco?
49428.e: Morocco's long west coast is on the Atlantic Ocean. There are many surfing beaches there.
49428.m: Morocco has a coast on the Atlantic to the west.

49429.q: What is a typical Moroccan dish cooked in a pot with a pointed lid called?
49429.e: A tagine is a clay pot with a pointed lid. The stew cooked in it is also called a tagine.
49429.m: In Morocco people often cook in a tagine with a pointed lid.

49430.q: What is the highest mountain in Kenya called?
49430.e: Mount Kenya is about 5,200 metres high. It is the highest mountain in the country and gave the country its name.
49430.m: Kenya's highest mountain is Mount Kenya.

49431.q: Which imaginary line around the Earth runs through Kenya?
49431.e: The equator divides the Earth into a northern and a southern half. It runs right through the middle of Kenya.
49431.m: The equator runs right through Kenya.

49432.q: Which ocean lies along the coast of Kenya?
49432.e: Kenya is in East Africa. Its coast, with the city of Mombasa, is on the Indian Ocean.
49432.m: Kenya has a coast on the Indian Ocean.

49433.q: Which wildlife reserve in Kenya is known for the great migration of wildebeest?
49433.e: Every year huge herds of wildebeest and zebras move into the Masai Mara. There they look for fresh grass.
49433.m: The Masai Mara in Kenya is famous for the wildebeest migration.

49434.q: Which people in Kenya are known for red cloths and high jumps when dancing?
49434.e: The Maasai live in Kenya and Tanzania. They often wear red cloths and dance with high jumps.
49434.m: The Maasai often wear red cloths and jump high when they dance.

49435.q: In which sport are athletes from Kenya especially successful?
49435.e: Runners from Kenya often win marathons and long races. Many train in the highlands.
49435.m: Kenya is famous for its fast long-distance runners.

49436.q: Apart from English, which language is an official language in Kenya?
49436.e: English and Swahili are the official languages in Kenya. Swahili is spoken in many countries of East Africa.
49436.m: In Kenya people speak Swahili and English.

49437.q: Which large lake borders Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania?
49437.e: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa. It is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.
49437.m: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa.

49438.q: What is the most famous national park in South Africa called?
49438.e: Lions, elephants, rhinos, buffalo and leopards live in Kruger National Park. It is one of the largest parks in Africa.
49438.m: Kruger National Park is the best-known park in South Africa.

49439.q: Which city is the largest city in South Africa?
49439.e: Johannesburg is the largest city in South Africa. It grew up after gold was found there.
49439.m: Johannesburg is the largest city in South Africa.

49440.q: In which year did South Africa host the Football World Cup?
49440.e: The 2010 World Cup was the first in Africa. Spain became world champions.
49440.m: The first Football World Cup in Africa took place in South Africa in 2010.

49441.q: Which valuable metal has been mined in South Africa for a long time?
49441.e: South Africa has large gold mines. Some of them are several kilometres deep.
49441.m: South Africa is known for its deep gold mines.

49442.q: Which animals can you see in the wild in South Africa?
49442.e: South Africa is at the southern tip of Africa. Lions, elephants, rhinos and giraffes live in its national parks.
49442.m: Lions and elephants live in South Africa.

49443.q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
49443.e: Abuja has been the capital of Nigeria since 1991. The city was built specially for this in the middle of the country.
49443.m: Abuja is the capital of Nigeria.

49444.q: Which city is the largest city in Nigeria?
49444.e: Lagos is on the coast and is the largest city in Nigeria. It used to be the capital too.
49444.m: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria.

49445.q: Which large river is Nigeria named after?
49445.e: The Niger flows through Nigeria and into the Atlantic. The country bears its name.
49445.m: Nigeria is named after the River Niger.

49446.q: What is the official language of Nigeria?
49446.e: Nigeria used to be a British colony. That is why English is the official language, and there are hundreds of other languages too.
49446.m: English is the official language in Nigeria.

49447.q: What colours is the flag of Nigeria?
49447.e: Nigeria's flag has three vertical stripes: green, white, green. Green stands for the land and nature.
49447.m: The flag of Nigeria is green and white.

49448.q: What is Nigeria's large film industry called?
49448.e: A great many films are made in Nigeria every year. This film industry is called Nollywood.
49448.m: Nigeria's film industry is called Nollywood.

49449.q: Which natural resource is especially important for Nigeria?
49449.e: Nigeria has large oil reserves. Oil is the country's most important export.

49450.q: What is the capital of Ethiopia?
49450.e: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia. The name means “new flower”.
49450.m: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia.

49451.q: Which drink originally comes from Ethiopia?
49451.e: The coffee plant originally comes from the highlands of Ethiopia. Coffee is still very important there today.

49452.q: What is the famous skeleton, over three million years old, that was found in Ethiopia called?
49452.e: Lucy was found in Ethiopia in 1974. She is one of the ancestors of humans and lived about 3.2 million years ago. Ötzi is much younger, and Sue is a dinosaur.
49452.m: The skeleton Lucy from Ethiopia is over three million years old.

49453.e: Ethiopia has no coast. Like Switzerland, it is a landlocked country.
49453.m: Ethiopia is not by the sea, just like Switzerland.

49454.q: What is the large, soft flatbread from Ethiopia called?
49454.e: Injera is a thin, slightly sour flatbread. People use it to eat their food, without any cutlery.
49454.m: In Ethiopia people eat injera, a soft flatbread.

49455.q: Which river starts at Lake Tana in Ethiopia?
49455.e: The Blue Nile flows out of Lake Tana. Later, in Sudan, it meets the White Nile, which comes from further south.
49455.m: The Blue Nile begins at Lake Tana in Ethiopia.

49456.q: How many months does the calendar in Ethiopia have?
49456.e: The Ethiopian calendar has twelve months of 30 days each. On top of that there is a short thirteenth month with 5 or 6 days.

49457.q: What is special about the old churches of Lalibela in Ethiopia?
a: They are carved out of the rock
They stand on stilts in the water
49457.e: In Lalibela, eleven churches were carved out of the rock about 800 years ago. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49457.m: Lalibela has churches carved out of the rock.

49458.q: Which animals can you watch in Gombe National Park in Tanzania?
49458.e: In Gombe National Park, Jane Goodall studied the chimpanzees for decades. They live there in the forest by the lake shore.
49458.m: Chimpanzees live in Gombe National Park in Tanzania.

49459.q: What is the money in Tanzania called?
49459.e: In Tanzania people pay with the Tanzanian shilling. Kenya and Uganda also have a currency called the shilling.
49459.m: In Tanzania people pay with the shilling.

49460.q: What is the well-known island off the coast of Tanzania called?
49460.e: Zanzibar belongs to Tanzania and lies in the Indian Ocean. The island is known for spices such as cloves.
49460.m: Zanzibar is a spice island belonging to Tanzania.

49461.q: Which large animals live in Tanzania's national parks?
49461.e: Tanzania is in Africa. Lots of elephants, lions, giraffes and zebras live in its national parks.
49461.m: Lots of elephants live in Tanzania.

49462.e: Tanzania is in the east of Africa. It has large national parks with lots of wild animals.

49463.q: Which city is the largest city in Tanzania?
49463.e: Dar es Salaam is on the Indian Ocean and is the largest city in Tanzania. It has the country's most important port.
49463.m: Dar es Salaam is the largest city in Tanzania.

49465.q: Which long and very deep lake lies on the western border of Tanzania?
49465.e: Lake Tanganyika is very long and one of the deepest lakes in the world. It lies between Tanzania and the Congo.
49465.m: Lake Tanganyika is one of the deepest lakes in the world.

49466.q: What is the capital of Ghana?
49466.e: Accra is the capital of Ghana. It is on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea.
49466.m: Accra is the capital of Ghana.

49467.q: Which raw material for chocolate is grown a lot in Ghana?
49467.e: Ghana is one of the largest cocoa producers in the world. Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.
49467.m: Ghana grows lots of cocoa for chocolate.

49468.q: What was Ghana called in the past, when it was a British colony?
49468.e: Ghana used to be called the Gold Coast. The name comes from the large amount of gold found there.
49468.m: Ghana used to be called the Gold Coast.

49469.q: In which year did Ghana become independent?
49469.e: Ghana became independent from Great Britain in 1957. It was one of the first countries in Africa to become free.

49470.q: What is the huge reservoir in Ghana called?
49470.e: Lake Volta was created by a dam on the River Volta. It is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world.
49470.m: Lake Volta in Ghana is a huge reservoir.

49471.q: What is the official language of Ghana?
49471.e: Because Ghana was a British colony, English is the official language. Many people also speak Twi.
49471.m: English is the official language in Ghana.

49472.q: What can you see in the middle of Ghana's flag?
49472.e: Ghana's flag has red, gold and green stripes. In the middle there is a black star.
49472.m: There is a black star on Ghana's flag.

49473.q: What is the capital of Senegal?
49473.e: Dakar is the capital of Senegal. It lies on a peninsula on the Atlantic.
49473.m: Dakar is the capital of Senegal.

49474.q: In which country is the westernmost point of mainland Africa?
49474.e: The westernmost point of mainland Africa is near Dakar in Senegal. It is called Pointe des Almadies.
49474.m: The westernmost point of mainland Africa is in Senegal.

49475.q: What is the official language of Senegal?
49475.e: Senegal used to be a French colony. That is why French is the official language, and many people also speak Wolof.
49475.m: French is the official language in Senegal.

49476.q: Which famous motor race used to end in the capital of Senegal?
49476.e: The Dakar Rally used to run from Europe right across the Sahara to Dakar. Today it takes place somewhere else.
49476.m: The Dakar Rally used to end in Senegal.

49477.q: What special colour is Lake Retba in Senegal often?
49477.e: Lake Retba is also called “Lac Rose”, the pink lake. Tiny algae in the very salty water turn it pink.
49477.m: Lake Retba in Senegal often glows pink.

49478.q: Which small country is almost completely surrounded by Senegal?
49478.e: Gambia lies like a narrow strip along a river. It is almost completely surrounded by Senegal.
49478.m: Gambia lies almost completely inside Senegal.

49479.q: Which thick tree is a symbol of Senegal?
49479.e: The baobab, also called the monkey-bread tree, has a very thick trunk. It appears on Senegal's coat of arms.
49479.m: The baobab is a symbol of Senegal.

49480.q: Which city is the capital of Egypt?
49480.e: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt. Over 20 million people live in the city and the area around it.
49480.m: Cairo is the capital of Egypt.

49481.q: Which famous ancient buildings stand right next to the city of Cairo in Egypt?
49481.e: Right on the edge of Cairo is Giza with the great pyramids. They are over 4,000 years old.
49481.m: The pyramids stand next to Cairo.

49482.q: Which language do most people in Cairo speak?
49482.e: In Cairo and all over Egypt people speak Arabic. It is the country's official language.

49483.q: What nickname does Cairo have because of its many mosques?
49483.e: A minaret is the tower of a mosque. Because Cairo has so many of them, it is called the “City of a Thousand Minarets”.
49483.m: Cairo is also called the “City of a Thousand Minarets”.

49484.q: There is a large bazaar in Cairo. What is a bazaar?
a: A market with lots of stalls
49484.e: A bazaar is a large market. In Cairo people sell spices, lamps and jewellery there.
49484.m: A bazaar is a large market.

49485.q: One of the oldest universities in the world is in Cairo. About how old is it?
49485.e: Al-Azhar in Cairo is over 1,000 years old. It is one of the oldest universities in the world.
49485.m: Cairo has a university that is over 1,000 years old.

49486.q: Which means of transport runs underground in Cairo?
49486.e: Cairo has had an underground railway, the Metro, since 1987. It was the first underground railway in Africa.
49486.m: Cairo has Africa's first underground railway.

49487.q: What is the flat mountain above Cape Town called?
49487.e: Table Mountain is completely flat on top, like a table. It is the landmark of Cape Town.
49487.m: Table Mountain is the landmark of Cape Town.

49488.q: How can you travel up Table Mountain in Cape Town in comfort?
a: by a lift inside the rock
49488.e: A cable car takes visitors up Table Mountain. Its cabin turns during the ride, so you can see all around.
49488.m: A cable car with a rotating cabin goes up Table Mountain.

49489.q: Which animals can you see at Boulders Beach near Cape Town?
49489.e: A colony of African penguins lives at Boulders Beach. You can watch them from close up.
49489.m: Penguins live on the beach near Cape Town.

49490.q: On which island off Cape Town was Nelson Mandela imprisoned for many years?
49490.e: Robben Island used to be a prison island. Today it is a museum and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49490.m: Nelson Mandela was imprisoned on Robben Island.

49491.q: Which well-known cape lies south of Cape Town?
49491.e: The Cape of Good Hope is on a peninsula south of Cape Town. Sailors sailed round it on the way to India.
49491.m: The Cape of Good Hope lies south of Cape Town.

49492.q: Which important South African institution is based in Cape Town?
49492.e: South Africa's Parliament meets in Cape Town. The government, however, works in Pretoria.
49492.m: South Africa's Parliament meets in Cape Town.

49493.q: What is the Bo-Kaap district in Cape Town known for?
49493.e: In the Bo-Kaap the houses are painted in bright colours. The district is a popular spot for photos.
49493.m: The Bo-Kaap in Cape Town has colourful houses.

49494.q: Which ocean is Cape Town on?
49494.e: Cape Town is on Table Bay on the Atlantic Ocean. The water there is often quite cool.
49494.m: Cape Town is on the Atlantic.

49495.q: Which city is the capital of Kenya?
49495.e: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya. It lies in the highlands in the south of the country.
49495.m: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

49496.q: What is special about the national park on the edge of Nairobi?
a: Wild animals in front of tower blocks
49496.e: Nairobi National Park is right next to the city. You can see giraffes and rhinos with tower blocks in the background.
49496.m: In Nairobi National Park you see wild animals in front of the city.

49497.q: What does the name Nairobi mean?
49497.e: The name comes from the Maa language. “Enkare Nairobi” means roughly “cool water”.

49498.q: At about what altitude is Nairobi?
49498.e: Nairobi lies in the highlands, at about 1,600 to 1,800 metres above sea level depending on the district. That is why it is quite mild there even though it is near the equator.
49498.m: Nairobi lies high up at about 1,700 metres.

49499.q: Which UN environmental organisation has its headquarters in Nairobi?
49499.e: UNEP is the United Nations Environment Programme. Its headquarters are in Nairobi.
49499.m: The UN Environment Programme is based in Nairobi.

49500.q: How did Nairobi begin towards the end of the 19th century?
a: as a camp for railway building
as a harbour by the sea
49500.e: Nairobi began in 1896 as a camp during the building of the Uganda Railway. The small camp soon became a big city.
49500.m: Nairobi began as a camp during the building of a railway.

49501.q: Which animals are raised in a well-known orphanage in Nairobi?
49501.e: In Nairobi National Park there is an orphanage for baby elephants. Later they are taken back to the wild.
49501.m: Orphaned elephants are raised in Nairobi.

49502.q: What is the largest of the pyramids of Giza called?
49502.e: The Pyramid of Khufu, also called the Great Pyramid, is the largest pyramid at Giza. It was built for the pharaoh Khufu.
49502.m: The Pyramid of Khufu is the largest pyramid at Giza.

49503.q: How many large pyramids stand at Giza?
49503.e: There are three large pyramids at Giza. They belong to the pharaohs Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure.
49503.m: There are three large pyramids at Giza.

49504.q: What were the pyramids of Giza built for?
49504.e: The pyramids were huge tombs. The pharaohs were meant to rest in them after their death.
49504.m: The pyramids were tombs for pharaohs.

49505.q: Which mythical creature with a lion's body and a human head lies in front of the pyramids?
49505.e: The Great Sphinx of Giza has the body of a lion and the head of a human. It is carved out of the rock.
49505.m: The Sphinx has a lion's body and a human head.

49506.q: What were the pyramids of Giza built from?
49506.e: The pyramids are made of millions of stone blocks, mainly limestone. Some blocks weigh several tonnes.
49506.m: The pyramids are built from huge stone blocks.

49507.q: About how tall was the Pyramid of Khufu originally?
49507.e: The Pyramid of Khufu was originally about 146 metres tall. Today it is a little lower because its tip is missing.
49507.m: The Pyramid of Khufu used to be about 146 metres tall.

49508.q: About how old are the pyramids of Giza?
49508.e: The pyramids were built more than 4,500 years ago. They are among the oldest buildings in the world.
49508.m: The pyramids of Giza are over 4,500 years old.

49509.q: Which material for writing on was invented in China?
49509.e: Paper was invented in China about 2,000 years ago. Later it reached Europe by way of Arabia.

49510.q: What is the main colour of China's flag?
49510.e: China's flag is red. At the top left there are yellow stars.
49510.m: China's flag is red with yellow stars.

49511.q: How many yellow stars are there on China's flag?
49511.e: On China's red flag there is one large and four small yellow stars. That makes 5 stars altogether.
49511.m: China's flag has five yellow stars.

49512.q: What is the longest river in China called?
49512.e: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and in the whole of Asia. It is over 6,000 kilometres long. The Yellow River is China's second-longest river.
49512.m: The Yangtze is the longest river in China.

49513.q: What do many people in China eat their food with?
49513.e: In China people often eat with two thin chopsticks. They are made of wood, bamboo or plastic.
49513.m: In China people often eat with chopsticks.

49514.q: Which big festival is celebrated in China in January or February?
49514.e: Chinese New Year is also called the Spring Festival. There are fireworks, red lanterns and dragon dances.
49514.m: In China the New Year festival is celebrated in January or February.

49515.q: Which language do most people in China speak?
49515.e: Most people in China speak Chinese. It is written with many characters instead of letters.
49515.m: In China people mainly speak Chinese.

49516.q: Which wrestling sport for heavy men is a national sport of Japan?
49516.e: In sumo, two heavy wrestlers try to push their opponent out of a circle. Sumo is very old and popular in Japan.
49516.m: Sumo is a form of wrestling from Japan.

49517.q: What does the flag of Japan look like?
49517.e: Japan's flag is white. In the middle there is a red circle that stands for the sun.
49517.m: Japan's flag is white with a red circle.

49518.q: What other name does Japan have?
49518.e: Seen from China, the sun rises in the east over Japan. That is why Japan is called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
49518.m: Japan is also called the Land of the Rising Sun.

49519.q: Which Japanese food is made of rice and often raw fish?
49519.e: Sushi is a well-known dish from Japan. It is made of rice and often topped with raw fish.
49519.m: Sushi is a Japanese food made of rice and fish.

49520.q: What is the very fast train in Japan called?
49520.e: The Shinkansen is Japan's high-speed train. It has been running since 1964 and is very punctual.
49520.m: The Shinkansen is Japan's high-speed train.

49521.q: What is the Japanese art of folding paper called?
49521.e: In origami you fold a sheet of paper into shapes, for example a crane. You do not need scissors.
49521.m: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

49522.q: What is the money in Japan called?
49522.e: In Japan people pay with the yen. Its symbol is ¥.
49522.m: In Japan people pay with yen.

49523.q: Which blossoms do people in Japan celebrate every spring?
49523.e: In spring the cherry trees in Japan blossom pink and white. Many families then have a picnic under the trees.
49523.m: In Japan people celebrate the cherry blossom in spring.

49524.e: “To” means east and “kyo” means capital. The name was chosen in 1868.

49525.q: About how many people live in the Greater Tokyo area?
49525.e: Well over 30 million people live in the Greater Tokyo area. That is more than three times as many as in the whole of Switzerland.
49525.m: Greater Tokyo is one of the largest urban areas in the world.

49526.q: Which city hosted the Summer Olympic Games that took place in 2021?
49526.e: The Games were called “Tokyo 2020”. Because of the coronavirus pandemic they only took place in summer 2021.
49526.m: The 2020 Summer Olympics took place in Tokyo in 2021.

49527.q: What was Tokyo called in the past?
49527.e: The city used to be called Edo. At that time it was the city of the powerful shoguns.
49527.m: Tokyo used to be called Edo.

49528.q: What is the tallest tower in Tokyo called?
49528.e: The Tokyo Skytree is 634 metres tall. It is the tallest tower in Japan. The older Tokyo Tower is much smaller.
49528.m: The Tokyo Skytree is the tallest tower in Japan.

49529.e: Tokyo is on Tokyo Bay. This bay is part of the Pacific Ocean.

49530.q: What is the Shibuya Crossing in Tokyo known for?
49530.e: At the Shibuya Crossing all the traffic lights turn green at the same time. Then thousands of people walk across the road in all directions.
49530.m: Huge numbers of pedestrians cross the Shibuya Crossing in Tokyo.

49531.q: What is the money in India called?
49531.e: In India people pay with the Indian rupee. Mahatma Gandhi is shown on the banknotes.
49531.m: In India people pay with rupees.

49532.q: Which river is sacred to many people in India?
49532.e: The Ganges is a sacred river for Hindus. Many people bathe in it to pray.
49532.m: The Ganges is a sacred river in India.

49533.q: What is the big film industry in the Indian city of Mumbai called?
49533.e: The name Bollywood is made from Bombay, the old name of Mumbai, and Hollywood. The films often have lots of music and dancing.
49533.m: Bollywood is the film industry in Mumbai.

49534.q: Which animal is considered sacred in Hinduism in India?
49534.e: In Hinduism the cow is sacred. That is why cows wander freely along the streets in India.
49534.m: In Hinduism the cow is considered sacred.

49535.q: Which sport is the most popular in India?
49535.e: Cricket is a game with a bat and ball. In India millions of people watch the matches.
49535.m: Cricket is the most popular sport in India.

49536.q: What is the heavy rainy season in India in summer called?
49536.e: The monsoon is a wind that brings lots of rain from the sea to India in summer. The farmers need the rain for their fields.
49536.m: The monsoon brings lots of rain to India in summer.

49537.q: Which large animal is the national animal of Thailand?
49537.e: The Asian elephant is Thailand's national animal. In the past elephants worked in the forest and carried heavy tree trunks.
49537.m: The elephant is Thailand's national animal.

49538.q: What is the money in Thailand called?
49538.e: In Thailand people pay with the baht. The king is shown on the banknotes.
49538.m: In Thailand people pay with baht.

49539.q: How do you greet someone politely in Thailand?
a: Put your hands together and bow
49539.e: The greeting in Thailand is called the wai. You put your palms together in front of your chest and bow your head.
49539.m: In Thailand people greet each other with their hands together and a bow.

49540.q: What is a tuk-tuk in Thailand?
49540.e: A tuk-tuk is a small, open taxi with three wheels. Its name comes from the sound of its engine.
49540.m: A tuk-tuk is a three-wheeled taxi.

49541.q: What religion do most people in Thailand follow?
49541.e: Most people in Thailand are Buddhists. The country has thousands of temples with golden Buddha figures.
49541.m: Most people in Thailand are Buddhists.

49542.q: About how many islands make up Indonesia?
49542.e: Indonesia is the largest island country in the world. It has over 17,000 islands, but nobody lives on many of them.
49542.m: Indonesia is made up of over 17,000 islands.

49543.q: Which city on the island of Java is the largest city in Indonesia?
49543.e: Jakarta is on the island of Java and has long been the capital. On the island of Borneo, Indonesia is building a new capital called Nusantara (as of 2025).
49543.m: Jakarta is the largest city in Indonesia.

49544.q: Which is the largest lizard in the world and lives in Indonesia?
49544.e: The Komodo dragon can grow to about 3 metres long. It only lives on a few islands in Indonesia.
49544.m: The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard in the world.

49545.q: Which ape with red fur lives in the rainforests of Asia?
49545.e: Orangutans live in the rainforests on large islands in Asia. Their name means “person of the forest”.
49545.m: The orangutan is an ape with red fur.

49546.q: Which country does the popular holiday island of Bali belong to?
49546.e: Bali is an Indonesian island with beaches, rice fields and many temples. Millions of holidaymakers come every year.
49546.m: Bali is a popular holiday island in Indonesia.

49547.q: Which volcano in Indonesia erupted violently in 1883?
49547.e: Krakatoa lies between the islands of Java and Sumatra. The bang from its eruption in 1883 could be heard very far away.

49548.q: Which imaginary line around the Earth runs right through Indonesia?
49548.e: The equator divides the Earth into a northern half and a southern half. It runs right through Indonesia, which is why it is always warm there.
49548.m: The equator runs right through Indonesia.

49549.q: What was Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam called in the past?
49549.e: Vietnam's largest city used to be called Saigon. Since 1976 it has been called Ho Chi Minh City.
49549.m: Ho Chi Minh City used to be called Saigon.

49550.q: What shape is Vietnam on the map?
a: Long and narrow like an S
49550.e: Vietnam is very long from north to south, but in some places only about 50 kilometres wide. It looks like an S.
49550.m: Vietnam is long and narrow like an S.

49551.q: What is Ha Long Bay in Vietnam famous for?
a: Lots of rocks in the sea
49551.e: In Ha Long Bay almost 2,000 limestone rocks rise out of the sea. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49551.m: In Ha Long Bay lots of rocks rise out of the sea.

49552.q: Which plant do farmers in Vietnam often grow in wet fields?
49552.e: Rice grows well in fields that are under water. Vietnam sells a great deal of rice to other countries.
49552.m: Lots of rice is grown in Vietnam.

49553.q: Which noodle soup is a typical dish from Vietnam?
49553.e: Pho is a soup with rice noodles, herbs and meat. In Vietnam people often eat it for breakfast.
49553.m: Pho is a noodle soup from Vietnam.

49554.q: Which large river flows into the sea in the south of Vietnam?
49554.e: The Mekong flows through several countries. In the south of Vietnam it splits into many branches and flows into the sea.
49554.m: The Mekong flows into the sea in Vietnam.

49555.q: What is the capital of South Korea?
49555.e: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea. About half of all the people in the country live in the greater Seoul area.
49555.m: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

49556.q: Which country borders South Korea to the north?
49556.e: Korea has been divided into two states since 1948. North Korea is in the north, South Korea in the south.
49556.m: North Korea lies north of South Korea.

49557.q: What is the spicy pickled cabbage dish from Korea called?
49557.e: Kimchi is cabbage pickled with chilli and garlic. In Korea people eat it with almost every meal.
49557.m: Kimchi is a spicy cabbage dish from Korea.

49558.q: Where did the 2018 Winter Olympics take place?
49558.e: The 2018 Winter Olympics were in Pyeongchang. That is a mountain region in South Korea.
49558.m: The 2018 Winter Olympics took place in South Korea.

49559.q: What is the Korean alphabet called?
49559.e: The Hangul alphabet was invented about 600 years ago. It has only a few letters and is easy to learn.
49559.m: The Korean alphabet is called Hangul.

49560.q: Which martial art comes from Korea?
49560.e: Taekwondo comes from Korea. Fighters mainly use fast kicks.
49560.m: Taekwondo is a martial art from Korea.

49561.q: What is the money in South Korea called?
49561.e: In South Korea people pay with the won. One Swiss franc is worth more than 1,000 won.
49561.m: In South Korea people pay with won.

49562.q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
49562.e: Ulaanbaatar is also spelled Ulan Bator. Almost half the people of Mongolia live there.
49562.m: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of Mongolia.

49563.q: What are people in Mongolia called who move from place to place with their herds?
49563.e: Nomads do not have a fixed house in one place. They move with their animals to wherever there is fresh grass.
49563.m: Nomads move from place to place with their herds.

49564.q: Which large desert lies in the south of Mongolia?
49564.e: The Gobi Desert is in Mongolia and China. It is hot there in summer and freezing cold in winter.
49564.m: The Gobi Desert is in Mongolia.

49565.q: What was the name of the famous ruler of the Mongols who founded a huge empire?
49565.e: About 800 years ago Genghis Khan united the Mongol peoples. He founded the Mongol Empire.
49565.m: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire.

49566.q: Which rare wild horse lives free in Mongolia again today?
49566.e: Przewalski's horse had almost died out in the wild. Zoos bred the animals and released them back into the wild in Mongolia.
49566.m: Przewalski's horse lives free in Mongolia again.

49567.q: Which animals are there far more of than people in Mongolia?
49567.e: In Mongolia many families keep large herds. There are many millions of sheep, but only about 3.5 million people.
49567.m: In Mongolia there are more sheep than people.

49568.q: Which contests take place at the Naadam festival in Mongolia?
49568.e: Naadam is the biggest festival in Mongolia. People compete in wrestling, horse racing and archery.
49568.m: At the Naadam festival there is riding, wrestling and archery.

49569.q: Which word do people use to greet each other in Nepal?
49569.e: In Nepal people say “Namaste”. While saying it, they put their hands together in front of their chest.
49569.m: In Nepal people greet each other with Namaste.

49570.q: What is the capital of Nepal?
49570.e: Kathmandu lies in a valley in the middle of Nepal. The city has many old temples.
49570.m: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.

49571.q: What is special about the flag of Nepal?
49571.e: Nepal's flag is made of two triangles one above the other. It is the only national flag that is not rectangular.

49572.q: What is the mountain people of Nepal called whose members often accompany climbers?
49572.e: The Sherpa live high in the mountains of Nepal. Many work as porters and mountain guides.
49572.m: The Sherpa often accompany climbers in Nepal.

49573.q: In which mountain range is the north of Nepal?
49573.e: The Himalayas are the highest mountains on Earth. Many of their highest peaks are in Nepal.

49574.q: In which place in Nepal was the Buddha born?
49574.e: According to tradition, the Buddha was born in Lumbini in the south of Nepal. Today the place is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49574.m: The Buddha was born in Lumbini in Nepal.

49575.q: Which long-haired kind of cattle lives high in the mountains of Nepal?
49575.e: The yak has thick, long fur against the cold. It carries loads and gives milk and wool.
49575.m: The yak is a long-haired kind of cattle.

49576.q: What is the capital of the Philippines?
49576.e: Manila is on the island of Luzon and is the capital of the Philippines. The city is very densely populated.
49576.m: Manila is the capital of the Philippines.

49577.q: About how many islands make up the Philippines?
49577.e: The Philippines are made up of over 7,000 islands. The largest are called Luzon and Mindanao.
49577.m: The Philippines are made up of over 7,000 islands.

49578.q: Who are the Philippines named after?
49578.e: The islands were named after Philip II, who later became King of Spain. Spain ruled the Philippines for over 300 years.
49578.m: The Philippines are named after the Spanish king Philip II.

49579.q: Which small animal with huge eyes lives in the Philippines?
49579.e: The Philippine tarsier is only as big as a hand. Its eyes are huge compared with its body.

49580.q: What are the colourful shared taxis in the Philippines called?
49580.e: Jeepneys were built from old army jeeps and painted in bright colours. They are a popular way to get around.
49580.m: Jeepneys are colourful shared taxis in the Philippines.

49581.q: What are the round hills on the island of Bohol that turn brown in the dry season called?
49581.e: There are over 1,000 round hills on Bohol. In the dry season the grass turns brown, and then they look like chocolate.
49581.m: The Chocolate Hills on Bohol look like chocolate.

49582.q: Which strong storms often hit the Philippines?
49582.e: A typhoon is a strong tropical storm over the Pacific. Several typhoons pass over the Philippines every year.
49582.m: The Philippines are often hit by typhoons.
