49583.q: Which country is Beijing the capital of?
49583.e: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China. In English it used to be called Peking.
49583.m: Beijing is the capital of China.

49584.q: What is the huge old imperial palace in Beijing called?
49584.e: The Chinese emperors used to live in the Forbidden City. Ordinary people were not allowed in, hence the name.
49584.m: The Forbidden City was the emperors' palace in Beijing.

49585.q: In which year did Beijing host the Summer Olympic Games?
49585.e: The 2008 Summer Olympics were in Beijing. The opening ceremony began on 8.8.2008.
49585.m: Beijing hosted the Summer Olympics in 2008.

49586.q: What is special about Beijing and the Olympic Games?
a: Both Summer and Winter Games took place there
The very first Olympic Games took place there
The Summer Games took place there three times
Only Winter Games took place there
49586.e: Beijing hosted the Summer Games in 2008 and the Winter Games in 2022 as well. No other city had managed that before.
49586.m: Both Summer and Winter Games took place in Beijing.

49587.q: What do you eat the famous Peking duck from China with?
49587.e: For Peking duck, the duck is roasted until crispy. It is eaten with thin pancakes and sauce.
49587.m: Peking duck is eaten with thin pancakes.

49588.q: What is the round temple in Beijing where the emperors prayed for a good harvest called?
49588.e: The emperors used to pray for a good harvest at the Temple of Heaven. The round hall has a blue roof.
49588.m: At the Temple of Heaven the emperors prayed for a good harvest.

49589.q: What does the Chinese name “Beijing” mean?
49589.e: “Bei” means north and “jing” means capital. The city is in the north of the country.

49590.q: Why was the Great Wall of China built?
49590.e: The wall was meant to protect the country from horse-riding peoples from the north. Soldiers guarded it.
49590.m: The Great Wall of China was meant to protect against attackers.

49591.q: How long is the Great Wall of China with all its parts together?
49591.e: A survey in 2012 found that all the sections together come to over 21,000 kilometres. It is the longest structure in the world.
49591.m: The Great Wall of China is over 20,000 kilometres long.

49592.q: Can you see the Great Wall of China from the moon with the naked eye?
49592.e: The wall is very long, but only a few metres wide. That is why you cannot see it from the moon.
49592.m: You cannot see the Great Wall of China from the moon.

49593.q: What stands at intervals along the Great Wall of China?
49593.e: There are many watchtowers on the wall. From them, soldiers could spot enemies early and send signals with smoke.
49593.m: There are many watchtowers on the Great Wall of China.

49594.q: How long did people spend building the Great Wall of China?
49594.e: Different emperors had the wall built over many centuries. The best-known parts are about 500 years old.
49594.m: The Great Wall of China was built over many hundreds of years.

49595.q: What are the best-known parts of the Great Wall of China built from?
49595.e: The best-known parts are made of stones and fired bricks. Older parts are made of rammed earth.
49595.m: The Great Wall of China is built of stone, bricks and earth.

49596.q: What do many tourists do on the Great Wall of China today?
49596.e: Every year millions of people walk along the wall. Some sections are very steep with lots of steps.
49596.m: You can walk along the Great Wall of China.

49597.q: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
49597.e: The Taj Mahal is in the north of India. It is one of the best-known buildings in the world.
49597.m: The Taj Mahal is in India.

49598.q: Why did a ruler have the Taj Mahal built?
a: As a tomb for his wife
As a palace to live in
As a temple for the gods
49598.e: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had the Taj Mahal built for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal. It is a sign of his love.
49598.m: The Taj Mahal is a tomb for a beloved wife.

49599.q: Which white stone is the Taj Mahal built from?
49599.e: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble. Depending on the light, it shimmers pink, white or golden.
49599.m: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble.

49600.q: Where does the Taj Mahal stand?
a: In the middle of the desert
49600.e: The Taj Mahal stands on the bank of a river in India. The river is called the Yamuna.
49600.m: The Taj Mahal stands by a river.

49601.q: Which famous list has the Taj Mahal been on since 2007?
a: New Seven Wonders of the World
Largest railway stations in the world
49601.e: In 2007 the “New Seven Wonders of the World” were chosen. The Taj Mahal is one of them.
49601.m: The Taj Mahal is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

49602.q: How many slender towers stand around the Taj Mahal?
49602.e: Four slender towers, the minarets, stand around the tomb. In the middle there is a large dome.
49602.m: Four towers stand around the Taj Mahal.

49603.q: What is the famous old fortress in the centre of the Russian capital called?
49603.e: The Kremlin is a fortress with high walls, towers and churches. The Russian president works there.
49603.m: The Kremlin is the famous fortress at the heart of Moscow.

49604.q: What is the money in Russia called?
49604.e: In Russia people pay with roubles. One rouble has 100 kopecks.
49604.m: In Russia people pay with roubles.

49605.q: What are the painted wooden dolls from Russia that fit inside each other called?
49605.e: A matryoshka is hollow inside. Inside it there is a smaller doll, inside that an even smaller one, and so on.
49605.m: The matryoshka is a Russian doll with many dolls inside.

49606.q: What is the huge, cold region in the Asian part of Russia called?
49606.e: Siberia stretches from the Urals to the Pacific. The winters there are very long and freezing cold.
49606.m: Siberia is a huge, cold region in Russia.

49607.q: What is the deepest lake in the world, which lies in Siberia, called?
49607.e: Lake Baikal is over 1,600 metres deep. It is also one of the oldest lakes on Earth.
49607.m: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world.

49608.q: What is the huge coniferous forest in Siberia called?
49608.e: The taiga is a forest of conifers such as spruces, pines and larches. It is the largest forest on Earth.
49608.m: The taiga is a huge coniferous forest in the north.

49609.q: What is the long railway line right across Siberia called?
49609.e: The Trans-Siberian Railway is over 9,000 kilometres long. It is the longest railway line in the world.
49609.m: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs right across Siberia.

49610.q: Which sea do Siberia's great rivers flow into?
49610.e: Great rivers such as the Ob, Yenisei and Lena flow north. They flow into the icy Arctic Ocean.
49610.m: Siberia's great rivers flow north into the Arctic Ocean.

49611.q: Which extinct animal is sometimes found well preserved in the ground in Siberia?
49611.e: Mammoths were large, hairy elephants of the Ice Age. Because the ground in Siberia is frozen, some mammoths have been preserved there as if in a fridge.
49611.m: Frozen mammoths are found in Siberia.

49612.q: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
49612.e: Riyadh lies in the middle of the desert. It is the capital and the largest city of the country.
49612.m: The capital of Saudi Arabia is Riyadh.

49613.q: On which peninsula is Saudi Arabia?
49613.e: Saudi Arabia covers most of the Arabian Peninsula. It lies between Africa and the rest of Asia.
49613.m: Saudi Arabia is on the Arabian Peninsula.

49614.q: Which city in Saudi Arabia is the holiest city of Islam?
49614.e: The Kaaba is in Mecca. Every year millions of Muslims go on pilgrimage there.
49614.m: Mecca is the holiest city of Islam.

49615.q: Which raw material made Saudi Arabia rich?
49615.e: Huge amounts of oil lie under the desert ground. Saudi Arabia sells it all over the world.
49615.m: Saudi Arabia became rich through oil.

49616.q: How many rivers that carry water all year round does Saudi Arabia have?
49616.e: Saudi Arabia is very dry and does not have a single river that always carries water. Drinking water comes from wells or from seawater with the salt removed.
49616.m: Saudi Arabia has no river that always carries water.

49617.q: What kind of landscape covers most of Saudi Arabia?
49617.e: Saudi Arabia is very hot and dry. Stony and sandy deserts cover most of the country.

49618.q: Which two seas does Saudi Arabia border?
49618.e: The Red Sea is to the west, the Persian Gulf to the east. In between there is a lot of desert.
49618.m: Saudi Arabia lies between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

49619.q: Which language is spoken in Saudi Arabia?
49619.e: Arabic is the official language of Saudi Arabia. It is written from right to left.
49619.m: In Saudi Arabia people speak Arabic.

49620.q: What is the capital of the United Arab Emirates?
49620.e: Abu Dhabi is the country's capital. But it is not the largest city.
49620.m: The capital of the United Arab Emirates is Abu Dhabi.

49621.q: How many emirates make up the United Arab Emirates?
49621.e: The United Arab Emirates are a federation of seven emirates. Each emirate has its own ruler.
49621.m: The United Arab Emirates are made up of seven emirates.

49622.q: What is the Palm Jumeirah in the United Arab Emirates?
49622.e: The Palm Jumeirah was built up out of sand in the sea. From above it looks like a palm tree.
49622.m: The Palm Jumeirah is an artificial island shaped like a palm tree.

49623.q: What is the money in the United Arab Emirates called?
49623.e: In the United Arab Emirates people pay with dirhams. One dirham has 100 fils.
49623.m: In the United Arab Emirates people pay with dirhams.

49624.q: Which bird is an important national symbol of the United Arab Emirates?
49624.e: Hunting with falcons has a long tradition in the Emirates. The falcon is even on the country's coat of arms.
49624.m: The falcon is a symbol of the United Arab Emirates.

49625.q: Which sea are the United Arab Emirates mainly on?
49625.e: Most of the big cities of the Emirates are on the coast of the Persian Gulf. The water there is very warm.
49625.m: The United Arab Emirates are on the Persian Gulf.

49626.q: On which continent are the United Arab Emirates?
49626.e: The Emirates are on the Arabian Peninsula. It belongs to the continent of Asia.
49626.m: The United Arab Emirates are in Asia.

49627.q: In which year were the United Arab Emirates founded?
49627.e: In 1971 the emirates joined together to form one state. Before that they were under British protection.
49627.m: The United Arab Emirates have existed since 1971.

49628.q: In which city is the Burj Khalifa?
49628.e: The Burj Khalifa is in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates. Dubai is the largest city in the country.
49628.m: The Burj Khalifa is in Dubai.

49629.q: In which year was the Burj Khalifa opened?
49629.e: Building it took about six years. The tower was opened in 2010.
49629.m: The Burj Khalifa was opened in 2010.

49630.q: What is special about the Burj Khalifa in Dubai?
a: It is the tallest building in the world
It is the longest bridge in the world
It is the oldest building in the world
It is the largest railway station in the world
49630.e: The Burj Khalifa is 828 metres tall. That is about four times as tall as the tallest building in Switzerland.
49630.m: The Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world.

49631.q: About how many floors does the Burj Khalifa have?
49631.e: The Burj Khalifa has over 160 floors. That makes it much taller than any other building.
49631.m: The Burj Khalifa has more than 160 floors.

49632.q: Who is the Burj Khalifa named after?
49632.e: The tower is named after Khalifa bin Zayed. He was President of the United Arab Emirates and ruler of Abu Dhabi.
49632.m: The Burj Khalifa bears the name of a ruler.

49633.q: Which sea is Israel on to the west?
49633.e: To the west Israel has a long coast on the Mediterranean. Big cities such as Tel Aviv and Haifa are there.

49634.q: What is the very salty lake between Israel and Jordan called, where you float on top almost by yourself?
49634.e: The water in the Dead Sea is about ten times saltier than normal seawater. That is why you float in it like a cork.
49634.m: You cannot sink in the Dead Sea.

49635.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Israel?
49635.e: Hebrew is the main language in Israel. Like Arabic, it is written from right to left.
49635.m: In Israel people mainly speak Hebrew.

49636.q: Which city is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims?
49636.e: Jerusalem has important holy places of three religions. They include the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Dome of the Rock.
49636.m: Jerusalem is a holy city for three religions.

49637.q: What is the money in Israel called?
49637.e: In Israel people pay with the new shekel. One shekel has 100 agorot.
49637.m: In Israel people pay with shekels.

49638.q: Which symbol can be seen on the flag of Israel?
49638.e: Israel's flag is white with two blue stripes. In the middle is a blue Star of David.
49638.m: There is a Star of David on Israel's flag.

49639.q: What is the desert in the south of Israel called?
49639.e: The Negev covers more than half of Israel. It is dry and stony.
49639.m: The Negev Desert is in the south of Israel.

49640.q: What is the freshwater lake in the north of Israel called?
49640.e: The Sea of Galilee is fed by the River Jordan. It is also often mentioned in the Bible.
49640.m: The Sea of Galilee is in the north of Israel.

49641.q: What is the capital of Jordan?
49641.e: Amman is the capital and largest city of Jordan. The city is built on many hills.
49641.m: The capital of Jordan is Amman.

49642.q: What is the desert with red rocks in the south of Jordan called?
49642.e: Wadi Rum is a desert valley with red sand and high rocks. Many films have been made there.
49642.m: Wadi Rum is a red rocky desert in Jordan.

49643.q: Which sea is Jordan's only port on?
49643.e: Jordan has only a short stretch of coast. The port city of Aqaba is there, on the Red Sea.
49643.m: Jordan has its port on the Red Sea.

49644.q: Which part of the world does Jordan belong to?
49644.e: Jordan is in western Asia, between Israel, Syria, Iraq and Saudi Arabia. This region is called the Middle East.
49644.m: Jordan is in the Middle East.

49645.e: The houses and tombs of Petra were carved directly into the rock walls. The city is over 2,000 years old.
49645.m: Petra is a city that was carved into the rock.

49646.q: What colour is the rock in Petra?
49646.e: Petra is carved out of sandstone that glows red and pink. That is why Petra is also called the rose-red city.
49646.m: The rock of Petra glows red and pink.

49647.q: Which Swiss man made Petra known in Europe in 1812?
49647.e: Johann Ludwig Burckhardt came from a Basel family. He travelled through the Middle East in Arab clothing and reached Petra in 1812.
49647.m: A Swiss man from a Basel family made Petra known in Europe.

49648.q: What is the most famous building in Petra called?
49648.e: The Treasury has a magnificent front with columns carved into the rock. It is about 2,000 years old.
49648.m: The Treasury is the most famous building in Petra.

49649.q: What is the capital of Iran?
49649.e: Tehran is the capital and the largest city of Iran. To the north of the city there are high mountains.
49649.m: The capital of Iran is Tehran.

49650.q: What was Iran usually called in Europe in the past?
49650.e: Until 1935 the country was mostly called Persia in Europe. Today its official name is Iran.
49650.m: Iran used to be called Persia.

49651.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Iran?
49651.e: The official language of Iran is Persian. It is also called Farsi.
49651.m: In Iran people mainly speak Persian.

49652.q: What has Iran been famous for for a long time?
49652.e: Persian carpets have been knotted by hand for centuries. They are known all over the world.
49652.m: Iran is famous for its carpets.

49653.q: Which expensive spice comes mainly from Iran?
49653.e: Saffron comes from the flowers of a kind of crocus. Most of the world's saffron comes from Iran.
49653.m: Most of the world's saffron comes from Iran.

49654.q: Which nuts are grown in especially large amounts in Iran?
49654.e: Iran is one of the biggest growers of pistachios. People like to eat the green kernels roasted.
49654.m: Lots of pistachios grow in Iran.

49655.q: What is the ancient ruined city of the Persian kings in Iran called?
49655.e: About 2,500 years ago Persepolis was a magnificent capital of the Persian kings. Today you can still see columns and staircases with carvings there.
49655.m: Persepolis was the city of the ancient Persian kings.

49656.q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
49656.e: Astana has been the capital of Kazakhstan since 1997. But the largest city in the country is Almaty.
49656.m: The capital of Kazakhstan is Astana.

49657.q: Kazakhstan is the largest country in the world without a ...?
49657.e: Kazakhstan has no access to the open sea. No other country without a coastline is as big.
49657.m: Kazakhstan is the largest country without a coastline.

49658.q: In 1961 the first person flew into space from Kazakhstan. What was his name?
49658.e: Yuri Gagarin took off on 12 April 1961 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. Baikonur is in Kazakhstan.
49658.m: Yuri Gagarin was the first person in space.

49659.q: What is the wide, flat grassland in Kazakhstan called?
49659.e: A large part of Kazakhstan is steppe. Mainly grasses grow there, and hardly any trees.

49660.q: Which fruit originally comes from the area around Kazakhstan?
49660.e: Wild apple trees grow in the mountains of Kazakhstan. Our apples are descended from them.
49660.m: The apple originally comes from Kazakhstan.

49661.q: Which bird do some Kazakhs hunt with, following an old tradition?
49661.e: Kazakhstan has an old tradition of hunting with golden eagles. The eagles catch foxes, for example.
49661.m: In Kazakhstan people traditionally hunt with golden eagles.

49662.q: Which country borders Kazakhstan to the north?
49662.e: Kazakhstan and Russia share a very long border. Until 1991 both were part of the Soviet Union.
49662.m: To the north, Kazakhstan borders Russia.

49663.q: Which large state was Kazakhstan part of until 1991?
49663.e: Kazakhstan was part of the Soviet Union. When it broke up in 1991, Kazakhstan became a country of its own.
49663.m: Kazakhstan has been a country of its own since 1991.

49664.q: What is the capital of Uzbekistan?
49664.e: Tashkent is the capital and the largest city of Uzbekistan. It is one of the largest cities in this region.
49664.m: The capital of Uzbekistan is Tashkent.

49665.q: Which famous old trading city with blue domes is in Uzbekistan?
49665.e: Samarkand is over 2,500 years old. The mosques and schools on Registan Square have magnificent blue domes.
49665.m: Samarkand is a famous old city in Uzbekistan.

49666.e: Uzbekistan is in the middle of Asia and has no coastline. Its neighbouring countries have no access to the open sea either.

49667.q: Which lake on the border of Uzbekistan has shrunk a great deal?
49667.e: A lot of water was taken from the rivers flowing into the Aral Sea for the fields. That is why most of the lake has dried up.
49667.m: The Aral Sea has shrunk a great deal.

49668.q: Which plant is grown in especially large amounts in Uzbekistan?
49668.e: Uzbekistan is one of the world's big cotton-growing countries. The fibres are used to make fabric for clothes.
49668.m: Lots of cotton is grown in Uzbekistan.

49669.q: What is plov, the national dish of Uzbekistan?
49669.e: Plov is rice with meat, carrots and onions. It is often cooked in a big pot.
49669.m: Plov is a rice dish from Uzbekistan.

49670.q: Which large state was Uzbekistan part of until 1991?
49670.e: Uzbekistan was part of the Soviet Union until 1991. After that it became a country of its own.

49671.q: Which part of the world does Uzbekistan belong to?
49671.e: Uzbekistan is in the middle of Asia, far from the oceans. That is why it counts as part of Central Asia.

49672.q: Which country did the silk on the Silk Road come from?
49672.e: The Chinese were the first to know how to make silk. For a long time they kept it a secret.

49673.q: Which famous traveller from Venice went along the Silk Road to China?
49673.e: Marco Polo travelled to China over 700 years ago. Later a book was written about his adventures.
49673.m: Marco Polo travelled along the Silk Road to China.

49674.q: What were the inns for traders and their animals on the Silk Road called?
49674.e: A caravanserai was a courtyard surrounded by walls. Traders and animals could stay the night there safely.
49674.m: Traders stayed the night in caravanserais.

49675.q: Apart from silk, which goods were traded on the Silk Road?
49675.e: Spices and precious stones were also traded. Potatoes, maize and tomatoes only came later, from America.
49675.m: Spices were also traded on the Silk Road.

49676.q: Which animal spins the threads that silk is made from?
49676.e: The caterpillar of the silk moth spins itself into a cocoon. Silk is made from this thread.
49676.m: Silk is made from the threads of a caterpillar.

49677.q: How many humps does the Bactrian camel, which often travelled the Silk Road, have?
49677.e: The Bactrian camel is a camel with two humps. It copes well with heat and with great cold too.
49677.m: The Bactrian camel has two humps.

49678.e: Dates contain a lot of sugar. That is why they taste very sweet.

49679.q: Where do date palms grow in the desert?
49679.e: An oasis is a place in the desert with water in the ground. Date palms can grow there.

49680.q: Which plant can be seen above two swords on the coat of arms of Saudi Arabia?
49680.e: Saudi Arabia's coat of arms shows a date palm and two crossed swords. The palm stands for growth and life.
49680.m: There is a palm tree on Saudi Arabia's coat of arms.

49681.e: Date palms come as male trees and female trees. Only the female trees bear dates.
49681.m: Only female date palms bear dates.

49682.q: How tall can a date palm grow?
49682.e: A date palm usually grows 15 to 20 metres tall. That is as tall as a building with about six floors.
49682.m: A date palm can grow about 20 metres tall.

49683.q: What are the large leaves of a palm called?
49683.e: Palms have long, feather-like leaves. These are called fronds.
49683.m: The leaves of a palm are called fronds.

49684.q: During Ramadan, what do many Muslims traditionally break their fast with in the evening?
49684.e: During the fasting month of Ramadan, Muslims eat nothing during the day. In the evening many first eat a date and drink water.
49684.m: During Ramadan the fast is often broken with a date.

49685.q: How do people in Switzerland usually buy dates?
49685.e: Dates do not grow in Switzerland. They are usually imported dried, which makes them keep for a long time.
49685.m: In Switzerland people usually eat dates dried.

50373.q: Which animal is a well-known symbol of France?
50373.e: The Gallic cockerel is an old symbol of France. You can see it, for example, on the shirts of French sports teams.
50373.m: The cockerel is a symbol of France.

50374.q: On which day does France celebrate its national day?
50374.e: On 14 July France celebrates with parades and fireworks. Switzerland celebrates its national day on 1 August.
50374.m: France celebrates its national day on 14 July.

50375.q: What is the highest mountain in France called?
50375.e: Mont Blanc is about 4800 metres high. It is the highest mountain in the Alps and lies on the border with Italy.
50375.m: Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in France.

50376.q: What is the long, thin bread typical of France called?
50376.e: The baguette is a long, narrow white loaf with a crunchy crust. In France people often buy it fresh from the baker every day.
50376.m: The baguette is a typical bread from France.

50377.q: Which large lake do Switzerland and France share?
50377.e: The southern shore of Lake Geneva belongs to France, the northern shore to Switzerland. In French it is called “Lac Léman”.
50377.m: Switzerland and France share Lake Geneva.

50378.q: For which event was the Eiffel Tower built?
50378.e: The tower was the entrance to a big world's fair in Paris. It was actually meant to be taken down again afterwards.
50378.m: The Eiffel Tower was built for a world's fair.

50379.q: Roughly how tall is the Eiffel Tower?
50379.e: With the aerials on top, the Eiffel Tower is about 330 metres tall (as of 2025). That is about as tall as a building with 100 floors.
50379.m: The Eiffel Tower is about 330 metres tall.

50380.q: How many levels for visitors does the Eiffel Tower have?
50380.e: Visitors can go up to three levels. The top one is very high and gives a wide view over Paris.
50380.m: The Eiffel Tower has three levels for visitors.

50381.q: What does the Eiffel Tower do every hour on the hour in the evening?
a: It turns round in a circle
50381.e: After sunset, thousands of lamps glitter for about five minutes every hour on the hour. It looks like twinkling stars.
50381.m: In the evening the Eiffel Tower sparkles every hour on the hour.

50382.q: Roughly every how many years is the Eiffel Tower repainted?
50382.e: To stop the iron rusting, the tower gets a new coat of paint about every seven years. This takes around 60 tonnes of paint.
50382.m: The Eiffel Tower is repainted about every seven years.

50383.q: What is the Louvre in Paris?
50383.e: The Louvre is a huge museum with paintings, statues and ancient treasures. It is one of the biggest museums in the world.
50383.m: The Louvre is a famous art museum.

50384.q: Which famous painting of a smiling woman hangs in the Louvre?
50384.e: The Mona Lisa is probably the most famous painting in the world. Every day lots of people stand in front of it to see her smile.
50384.m: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre.

50385.q: How is the most famous painting in the Louvre protected from damage?
50385.e: The famous painting is small and very valuable. That is why it hangs behind thick bulletproof glass that can also withstand blows.
50385.m: The most valuable painting in the Louvre hangs behind bulletproof glass.

50386.q: What stands in front of the entrance to the Louvre?
50386.e: A large glass pyramid stands in front of the Louvre. The museum's main entrance is underneath it.
50386.m: A glass pyramid stands in front of the Louvre.

50387.q: What was the Louvre before it became a museum?
50387.e: The Louvre used to be a castle and later a palace where kings of France lived. Only later were works of art put there for everyone.
50387.m: The Louvre used to be a palace of the kings.

50388.q: Which art museum has more visitors than any other in the world?
50388.e: The Louvre is the most visited museum in the world. Around 9 million people come every year (as of 2024).
50388.m: The Louvre is the most visited museum in the world.

50389.q: Which famous statue without arms stands in the Louvre?
50389.e: The Venus de Milo is an ancient marble statue from Greece. Its arms have been missing ever since it was discovered.
50389.m: The Venus de Milo stands in the Louvre.

50390.q: Which famous painting hangs in the Louvre in Paris?
50390.e: The Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci is the best-known painting in the Louvre. The museum has been open to everyone since 1793.
50390.m: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre.

a: A rock with a monastery in the sea
A high mountain in the Alps
50391.e: Mont-Saint-Michel is a small rocky island off the coast of France. At the very top there is an old monastery with a church.
50391.m: There is a monastery in the sea on Mont-Saint-Michel.

50392.q: In which region of France is Mont-Saint-Michel?
50392.e: Mont-Saint-Michel is in Normandy in northern France. There it is very close to the border with Brittany.

50393.q: What lies below the monastery on Mont-Saint-Michel?
a: A small village with narrow lanes
50393.e: On the slope below the monastery there is a small village with a steep, narrow main street. There are shops, restaurants and old houses.
50393.m: A small village lies below the monastery.

50394.q: Which golden figure stands at the very top of the spire of Mont-Saint-Michel?
50394.e: At the top stands a golden figure of the Archangel Michael. The whole mount is named after him.
50394.m: The Archangel Michael stands on top of the spire.

50395.q: How do you get to Mont-Saint-Michel on foot today?
50395.e: Since 2014, a long bridge has led from the mainland to the rock. That way you can cross with dry feet even at high tide.
50395.m: A bridge connects Mont-Saint-Michel with the mainland.

50396.e: Since 1979, Mont-Saint-Michel and its bay have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Such places are considered especially valuable for all of humanity.
50396.m: Mont-Saint-Michel is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

50397.q: Which dish is especially famous on Mont-Saint-Michel?
50397.e: A restaurant on the rock has long been famous for its big, fluffy omelette. The eggs are beaten for a long time there.
50397.m: The omelette is famous on Mont-Saint-Michel.

50398.q: Who used to live in the monastery on Mont-Saint-Michel?
50398.e: Monks lived in the monastery for many centuries. They prayed there and kept extending the church.
50398.m: Monks used to live in the monastery on Mont-Saint-Michel.

50399.q: How many official languages does Belgium have?
50399.e: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German. Switzerland even has four national languages.

50400.q: Which baked treat with a grid pattern is Belgium known for?
50400.e: Belgian waffles have a pattern of small squares. They are often eaten with icing sugar, fruit or cream.
50400.m: Belgium is known for its waffles.

50401.q: Which filled chocolate sweet was invented in Belgium?
50401.e: The praline was invented in Belgium in 1912. It is made of a chocolate shell with a soft filling.
50401.m: The praline was invented in Belgium.

50402.q: What colours is the flag of Belgium?
50402.e: The Belgian flag has three vertical stripes in black, yellow and red. The colours come from old coats of arms of the country.
50402.m: The flag of Belgium is black, yellow and red.

50403.q: Which country do the Smurfs come from?
50403.e: The little blue Smurfs were created by the Belgian artist Peyo. They first appeared in a comic in 1958.

50404.q: Who is at the head of the country of Belgium?
50404.e: Belgium is a kingdom. Philippe has been King of the Belgians since 2013 (as of 2025).
50404.m: Belgium is led by a king.

50405.q: Which Belgian city is famous for trading diamonds?
50405.e: Diamonds have been traded and cut in Antwerp for centuries. The city also has a large port.
50405.m: Antwerp is the city of diamonds.

50406.q: Which country is a neighbour of Belgium?
50406.e: Belgium borders France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. To the north lies the North Sea.
50406.m: France is a neighbour of Belgium.

50407.q: What is the capital of Belgium?
50407.e: Brussels is the capital of Belgium. The king and his family also live there.
50407.m: Brussels is the capital of Belgium.

50408.q: What is the name of the small fountain statue of a boy that is very famous in Brussels?
50408.e: Manneken Pis is a bronze statue of a boy weeing, only about 60 centimetres tall. He owns more than 900 costumes, which he wears in turn.
50408.m: Manneken Pis is a famous statue in Brussels.

50409.q: Which building in Brussels is made of huge shiny balls?
50409.e: The Atomium was built in 1958 for a world fair. It shows a tiny building block of iron enlarged many billions of times.
50409.m: The Atomium in Brussels is made of big balls.

50410.q: Every two years a huge carpet lies on the big square in Brussels. What is it made of?
50410.e: Every two years in August, a carpet made of many thousands of flowers lies on the Grand-Place in Brussels.
50410.m: Brussels has a flower carpet every two years.

50411.q: Which group of countries has important buildings in Brussels?
50411.e: Important parts of the European Union work in Brussels, for example the European Commission. The Olympic Committee, FIFA and the Red Cross, on the other hand, have their headquarters in Switzerland.
50411.m: The European Union works in Brussels.

50412.q: Which two languages are official languages in Brussels?
50412.e: In Brussels, street signs are usually in two languages, French and Dutch. In everyday life you hear French the most.
50412.m: In Brussels people speak French and Dutch.

50413.q: What is painted on many house walls in Brussels?
50413.e: Brussels is known as the city of comics. Big pictures of famous comic characters are painted on many house walls.
50413.m: In Brussels you can see comic pictures on many house walls.

50414.q: What can you see in the Mini-Europe park in Brussels?
50414.e: In the Mini-Europe park, many well-known buildings from Europe stand as small models. Swissminiatur in Ticino is a similar park.
50414.m: Mini-Europe shows Europe's buildings in miniature.

50415.q: In which city does the government of the Netherlands work?
50415.e: The government and parliament of the Netherlands are based in The Hague. The king also lives there.
50415.m: The government of the Netherlands works in The Hague.

50416.q: What do many people call the Netherlands, even though it is only part of the country?
50416.e: Holland is really only a region in the west of the country with two provinces. Even so, many people say “Holland” for the whole country.
50416.m: Holland is only part of the Netherlands.

50417.q: Which language is spoken in the Netherlands?
50417.e: People in the Netherlands speak Dutch. It is related to German, so some words sound similar.
50417.m: Dutch is spoken in the Netherlands.

50418.q: What is special about many areas of the Netherlands?
a: They lie lower than the sea
50418.e: About a quarter of the country lies below sea level. Without protection, the sea would flood the land there.
50418.m: Many areas of the Netherlands lie lower than the sea.

50419.q: What protects the land in the Netherlands from the sea?
50419.e: Dykes are long, high banks of earth along the coast and the rivers. They keep the water away from the land.
50419.m: Dykes protect the Netherlands from the sea.

50420.q: Which means of transport do people in the Netherlands use especially often?
50420.e: There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands. The country is flat and has a great many cycle paths.
50420.m: Lots of people in the Netherlands ride bicycles.

50421.q: What colour do Dutch fans wear at sports events?
50421.e: Orange is the colour of the royal family, which is called the “House of Orange”. That is why fans of the Netherlands wear orange.
50421.m: Fans of the Netherlands wear orange.

50422.q: Which kind of cheese is named after a town in the Netherlands?
50422.e: Gouda is a town in the Netherlands whose market has traded cheese for a long time. Emmental, on the other hand, comes from Switzerland.
50422.m: Gouda is a cheese from the Netherlands.

50423.q: What are the traditional Dutch shoes, called klompen, made of?
50423.e: Klompen are carved from a single piece of wood. In the past, farmers wore them for work in wet fields.

50424.q: What do the old houses along the canals in Amsterdam often look like?
50424.e: It is often said that taxes used to depend on how wide a house was along the canal. So houses were built narrow, but tall and deep.
50424.m: The old canal houses are narrow and tall.

50425.q: What are the grachten in Amsterdam?
50425.e: Grachten are canals that run like rings through the old town. In the past, ships carried goods along them right up to the houses.

50426.q: Roughly how many bridges are there in Amsterdam?
50426.e: Because there are so many canals, Amsterdam needs a great many bridges. There are well over 1,000.

50427.q: What do some people live on in the canals of Amsterdam?
50427.e: There are around 2,500 houseboats on the canals. People live in them just like in a flat.
50427.m: Some people in Amsterdam live on houseboats.

50428.q: Whose hiding place can you visit in a museum in Amsterdam?
50428.e: Anne Frank was a Jewish girl who had to hide with her family in a back building during the Second World War. There she wrote her famous diary.
50428.m: In Amsterdam you can visit Anne Frank's hiding place.

50429.q: Which painter is a famous museum in Amsterdam named after?
50429.e: The Van Gogh Museum has many of the painter's pictures, for example his sunflowers. He came from the Netherlands.
50429.m: Amsterdam has a museum for Vincent van Gogh.

50430.q: Which painter painted the large picture “The Night Watch”, which hangs in Amsterdam?
50430.e: Rembrandt was a famous painter from the Netherlands. “The Night Watch” hangs in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

50431.q: What is the hook at the top of many old houses in Amsterdam for?
50431.e: The stairs in the old houses are very steep. So large furniture is pulled up the outside with a rope on the hook and brought in through the window.
50431.m: The hook on the house is used to lift furniture.

50432.q: Which river is Amsterdam named after?
50432.e: The city grew up at a dam on the River Amstel. That is why it is called Amsterdam.
50432.m: Amsterdam is named after the River Amstel.

50433.q: What were many windmills in the Netherlands used for?
50433.e: Many mills pumped water from the low land into the canals. This kept fields and villages dry.
50433.m: Windmills in the Netherlands pumped water away.

50434.q: What did windmills often grind in the past?
50434.e: Heavy millstones turned in many windmills. They ground grain into flour for bread.

50435.q: At which place in the Netherlands do 19 old windmills stand close together?
50435.e: In Kinderdijk, 19 old windmills stand along canals. They have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
50435.m: There are 19 old windmills at Kinderdijk.

50436.q: How many sails does a typical windmill in the Netherlands have?
50436.e: Most old windmills have four large sails. The wind turns them and so drives the mill.
50436.m: A typical windmill has four sails.

50437.q: What do modern wind turbines produce?
50437.e: Modern wind turbines turn a generator that produces electricity. There are also some wind turbines in Switzerland, for example in the Jura.

50438.q: What does a tulip grow from?
50438.e: Tulips grow from flower bulbs that are planted in the ground in autumn. Food for the plant is stored in the bulb.
50438.m: A tulip grows from a bulb.

50439.q: In which season do tulips flower?
50439.e: Tulips are among the first colourful flowers of the year. They usually flower in April and May.

50440.q: What is the name of the famous flower park in the Netherlands with millions of tulips?
50440.e: Every spring, millions of flowers bloom at Keukenhof, mostly tulips. The park is only open for a few weeks a year.
50440.m: Keukenhof is a famous tulip park.

50441.q: What was going on with tulip bulbs in Holland almost 400 years ago?
50441.e: Around 1637, rare tulip bulbs were so sought after that some cost more than a house. This is called “tulip mania”.
50441.m: Tulip bulbs used to be very expensive in Holland.

50442.q: What is the capital of Luxembourg?
50442.e: The capital has the same name as the country. The city of Luxembourg sits on rocks above deep valleys.
50442.m: The capital of Luxembourg is also called Luxembourg.

50443.q: What kind of country is Luxembourg?
50443.e: Luxembourg is the only grand duchy in the world. A grand duke is at its head.

50444.q: Which language of their own do people in Luxembourg speak with each other?
50444.e: Luxembourgers speak Luxembourgish with each other. French and German are also official languages.
50444.m: Luxembourgish is the language of the Luxembourgers.

50445.q: How big is Luxembourg compared with Switzerland?
50445.e: Luxembourg is about 16 times smaller than Switzerland. It is roughly the size of the canton of Ticino.
50445.m: Luxembourg is much smaller than Switzerland.

50446.q: Which country is NOT a neighbour of Luxembourg?
50446.e: Luxembourg only borders Belgium, France and Germany. The Netherlands lies further north.
50446.m: Luxembourg borders Belgium, France and Germany.

50447.q: What has been free in Luxembourg since 2020?
50447.e: Since 2020, you can travel by bus, tram and train all over Luxembourg without a ticket. Luxembourg was the first country in the world to do this.
50447.m: In Luxembourg, buses and trains are free.

50448.q: What colours is the flag of Luxembourg?
50448.e: The flag has three horizontal stripes in red, white and light blue. It looks very similar to the flag of the Netherlands, only the blue is lighter.
50448.m: The flag of Luxembourg is red, white and light blue.

50449.q: What are the casemates in the city of Luxembourg?
50449.e: The casemates are long passages that were dug into the rock long ago. Soldiers could shelter there.
50449.m: The casemates are passages in the rock of Luxembourg.

50450.q: What does the name “Côte d'Azur” mean in English?
50450.e: “Côte” means coast and “azur” is a bright sky blue. The name suits the blue sea and sky.
50450.m: Côte d'Azur means Blue Coast in English.

50451.q: Which sea is the Côte d'Azur on?
50451.e: The Côte d'Azur is in the south-east of France on the Mediterranean. The water there is warm in summer.
50451.m: The Côte d'Azur is on the Mediterranean.

50452.q: Which is the largest city on the Côte d'Azur?
50452.e: Nice has around 340,000 inhabitants and is the largest city on this coast. It also has a large airport.
50452.m: Nice is the largest city on the Côte d'Azur.

50453.q: In which town on the Côte d'Azur is a famous film festival held every year?
50453.e: Film stars from all over the world meet in Cannes every May. Locarno in Ticino also has a well-known film festival, but not by the sea.
50453.m: Cannes has a famous film festival.

50454.q: In which city is the famous seafront promenade “Promenade des Anglais”?
50454.e: The Promenade des Anglais is a long path right by the sea in Nice. The name means “Promenade of the English”.
50454.m: The Promenade des Anglais is in Nice.

50455.q: What is the weather usually like on the Côte d'Azur in summer?
50455.e: The Côte d'Azur has a great many sunny days a year. The summers are hot and dry, the winters mild.
50455.m: On the Côte d'Azur it is usually warm and sunny in summer.

50456.q: Which mountains reach close to the sea on the Côte d'Azur?
50456.e: The Maritime Alps are the southernmost part of the Alps. They reach almost to the coast, so there you can swim and ski on the same day.
50456.m: On the Côte d'Azur the Alps reach close to the sea.

50457.q: What are many beaches on the Côte d'Azur made of?
50457.e: Many beaches there are made of round, smooth pebbles instead of fine sand. So beach shoes are handy.
50457.m: Many beaches on the Côte d'Azur have pebbles.

50458.e: Monaco is a principality. Albert II has been the Prince of Monaco since 2005 (as of 2025).
50458.m: Monaco is ruled by a prince.

50459.q: What can you watch every day in front of the Prince's Palace in Monaco?
50459.e: Every day shortly before noon, the guards in front of the palace change in a small ceremony. Many tourists watch.
50459.m: There is a changing of the guard in front of the Prince's Palace every day.

50460.q: Which motor race goes through the streets of Monaco every year?
50460.e: At the Monaco Grand Prix, Formula 1 cars race through narrow streets and bends. The track even goes through a tunnel.
50460.m: Formula 1 races through the streets of Monaco.

50461.q: What is the name of a well-known district of Monaco with a famous casino?
50461.e: Monte Carlo is a district of Monaco. It has a magnificent casino and many luxury hotels.
50461.m: Monte Carlo is a district of Monaco.

50462.q: Which country does Monaco border on land?
50462.e: On the land side, Monaco is completely surrounded by France. On the other side is the sea.

50463.q: What colours is the flag of Monaco?
50463.e: The flag of Monaco is red at the top and white at the bottom. These are the colours of the princely family.
50463.m: The flag of Monaco is red and white.

50464.q: Which famous museum in Monaco shows fish and other sea creatures?
50464.e: The Oceanographic Museum stands on a cliff right above the sea. It has a large aquarium with many sea creatures.
50464.m: In Monaco, the Oceanographic Museum shows sea creatures.

50465.q: What money do you pay with in Monaco?
50465.e: Monaco is not part of the European Union but still uses the euro. It is even allowed to mint its own euro coins.
50465.m: In Monaco you pay with euros.

50466.q: How many horses pull the chariot on the Brandenburg Gate?
50466.e: The chariot on top of the gate is pulled by four horses. A chariot with four horses is called a quadriga.

50467.q: Who drives the chariot on the Brandenburg Gate?
50467.e: Victoria, the goddess of victory, stands on the chariot. She holds a staff with an eagle.
50467.m: Victoria, the goddess of victory, drives the quadriga.

50468.q: What is the Brandenburg Gate built from?
50468.e: The gate was built from light sandstone more than 200 years ago.
50468.m: The Brandenburg Gate is made of sandstone.

50469.q: What used to stand right next to the Brandenburg Gate and divided Berlin into two parts?
50469.e: For almost 30 years, the Berlin Wall stood right next to the gate. Since the fall of the Wall in 1989, people can walk through it again.
50469.m: The Berlin Wall used to stand by the Brandenburg Gate.

50470.q: Which celebration do many people mark every year with fireworks in front of the Brandenburg Gate?
50470.e: On the night before 1 January there is a big New Year's Eve party with fireworks in front of the gate.
50470.m: People celebrate New Year's Eve in front of the Brandenburg Gate.

50472.q: Which German city has the largest port in Germany?
50472.e: Hamburg has the largest port in Germany. Every day, big ships from all over the world arrive there.
50472.m: Germany's largest port is in Hamburg.

50473.q: Which river is the port of Hamburg on?
50473.e: The port of Hamburg is on the Elbe. The ships travel along the river to the sea.

50474.q: What are the big metal boxes that ships use to carry goods called?
50474.e: Containers are big boxes made of metal. They fit on ships, lorries and trains.
50474.m: Containers are big boxes for goods.

50475.q: What is used to lift the containers off the ships in the port of Hamburg?
50475.e: Huge cranes lift the heavy containers off the ship and put them down on land.
50475.m: Cranes lift containers off the ships.

50476.q: What is the old district of red-brick warehouses at the port of Hamburg called?
50476.e: Coffee, tea and spices used to be stored in the Speicherstadt. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2015.
50476.m: The Speicherstadt is an old warehouse district in Hamburg.

50477.q: Which famous concert hall with a wavy glass roof stands at the port of Hamburg?
50477.e: The Elbphilharmonie stands on top of an old warehouse. Its roof looks like waves.
50477.m: The Elbphilharmonie is a concert hall at the port of Hamburg.

50478.q: Which market takes place at the port in Hamburg early every Sunday morning?
50478.e: The Hamburg fish market starts very early on Sundays. It sells not only fish but also fruit and much more.
50478.m: Hamburg has its fish market on Sunday mornings.

50479.q: Which big festival does Hamburg celebrate at the port every year in May?
50479.e: Many ships and visitors come for the port's birthday. There are parades on the water and fireworks.
50479.m: Hamburg celebrates the port's birthday every year.

50480.q: Which sea do ships sail into when they leave the port of Hamburg?
50480.e: The river at Hamburg flows into the North Sea. From there, ships sail all over the world.
50480.m: Ships from the port of Hamburg sail into the North Sea.

50481.q: Which big folk festival takes place in Munich every year?
50481.e: Oktoberfest is one of the biggest folk festivals in the world. It actually starts in September.

50482.q: Munich is the capital of which German state?
50482.e: Munich is the capital of Bavaria. Bavaria is in the south of Germany.
50482.m: Munich is the capital of Bavaria.

50483.q: What is the most famous square in the centre of Munich called?
50483.e: Marienplatz is the centre of Munich. The New Town Hall stands there.
50483.m: Marienplatz is in the centre of Munich.

50484.q: What dances to music in the tower of Munich's town hall?
50484.e: There is a glockenspiel in the tower of the New Town Hall. Colourful figures turn and dance to it.
50484.m: Figures dance at the glockenspiel in Munich.

50485.q: How many towers does the Frauenkirche in Munich have?
50485.e: The Frauenkirche has two towers with round domes. They are a landmark of Munich.

50486.e: The Isar flows through Munich. In summer, lots of people lie in the sun on its banks.

50487.q: What is the huge park in Munich called?
50487.e: The English Garden is one of the largest city parks in the world. It is even bigger than Central Park in New York.
50487.m: The big park in Munich is called the English Garden.

50488.q: What can you see at Hellabrunn Zoo in Munich?
a: Animals from all over the world
50488.e: Hellabrunn Zoo is in the south of Munich on the Isar. Animals from all over the world live there.
50488.m: Animals from all over the world live at Hellabrunn Zoo in Munich.

50489.q: What is the big museum of technology and science in Munich called?
50489.e: The Deutsches Museum is one of the largest technology museums in the world. You can see aeroplanes, ships and mines there.
50489.m: The Deutsches Museum in Munich shows technology.

50490.q: Which king had Neuschwanstein Castle built?
50490.e: King Ludwig II of Bavaria had the castle built. He is also called the Fairy Tale King.
50490.m: King Ludwig II had Neuschwanstein built.

50491.q: In which country is Neuschwanstein Castle?
50491.e: Neuschwanstein is in the south of Germany, near the border with Austria.

50492.q: What is Neuschwanstein often called because of how it looks?
50492.e: With its many white towers, Neuschwanstein looks like a castle from a fairy tale.
50492.m: Neuschwanstein is called a fairy-tale castle.

50493.q: Neuschwanstein Castle stands at the edge of which mountain range?
50493.e: The castle stands on a rock in front of the mountains of the Alps.
50493.m: Neuschwanstein stands at the edge of the Alps.

50494.q: The wall paintings in Neuschwanstein show stories from the operas of which composer?
50494.e: The king was a great fan of Richard Wagner's operas. So many pictures in the castle show legends from these operas.
50494.m: Neuschwanstein Castle has paintings about Wagner's operas.

50495.q: Was Neuschwanstein Castle ever completely finished?
50495.e: When the king died in 1886, the castle was not yet finished. Many rooms stayed empty.

50497.q: How long did the king live in Neuschwanstein Castle?
50497.e: Altogether the king lived in the castle for only about 170 days. Shortly afterwards he died.
50497.m: The king only lived in Neuschwanstein for a short time.

50498.q: Which kind of clock is typical of the Black Forest?
50498.e: Cuckoo clocks have been made in the Black Forest for a long time. Every full hour, a little bird calls out.
50498.m: The cuckoo clock comes from the Black Forest.

50499.q: Apart from cherries, what goes into a Black Forest gateau?
50499.e: A Black Forest gateau has layers of chocolate sponge, cream and cherries.
50499.m: Black Forest gateau is made with cherries and cream.

50500.q: What is on the famous Bollenhut hat from the Black Forest?
50500.e: The Bollenhut has big pompoms made of wool. Red pompoms are worn by women who are not yet married.

50501.q: Which trees make the Black Forest so dark?
50501.e: Many dark conifers such as firs and spruces grow in the Black Forest. That is why the forest looks almost black.
50501.m: Dark firs and spruces give the Black Forest its name.

50502.q: Which big river has its source in the Black Forest?
50502.e: The Danube begins in the Black Forest from two streams. It then flows right across Europe to the Black Sea.
50502.m: The Danube has its source in the Black Forest.

50503.q: What is the highest mountain in the Black Forest called?
50503.e: The Feldberg is around 1,500 metres high. In winter you can ski there.
50503.m: The Feldberg is the highest mountain in the Black Forest.

50504.q: In which German state is the Black Forest?
50504.e: The Black Forest is in the south-west of Germany, in the state of Baden-Württemberg.
50504.m: The Black Forest is in Baden-Württemberg.

50505.q: Which country does the Black Forest border in the south?
50505.e: In the south, the Black Forest ends at the Rhine. On the other side of the river is Switzerland.
50505.m: The Black Forest is close to Switzerland.

50506.q: Which city lies on the edge of the Black Forest?
50506.e: Freiburg im Breisgau lies right next to the Black Forest. You can get there quickly from Basel.
50506.m: Freiburg im Breisgau lies by the Black Forest.

50507.q: In which city is St Stephen's Cathedral?
50507.e: St Stephen's Cathedral stands in the middle of Vienna's old town. It is the city's landmark.
50507.m: St Stephen's Cathedral is the landmark of Vienna.

50508.q: What do the people of Vienna lovingly call St Stephen's Cathedral?
50508.e: The people of Vienna lovingly call their cathedral “Steffl”.
50508.m: In Vienna, St Stephen's Cathedral is also called Steffl.

50509.q: What is special about the roof of St Stephen's Cathedral?
a: It is made entirely of gold
50509.e: The roof is covered with many colourful tiles. They form zigzag patterns and eagles.
50509.m: St Stephen's Cathedral has a colourful tiled roof.

50510.q: What is the biggest bell of St Stephen's Cathedral called?
50510.e: The Pummerin is the biggest bell in Austria. It only rings on special occasions, for example at New Year.
50510.m: The Pummerin is the biggest bell in St Stephen's Cathedral.

50511.q: Roughly how tall is the south tower of St Stephen's Cathedral?
50511.e: The south tower is about 136 metres tall. It is one of the tallest church towers in Europe.
50511.m: The south tower of St Stephen's Cathedral is around 136 metres tall.

50512.q: Which tower of St Stephen's Cathedral is much taller?
50512.e: The north tower was never finished. That is why the south tower is much taller.
50512.m: The south tower is the tallest tower of St Stephen's Cathedral.

50513.q: On which square does St Stephen's Cathedral stand?
50513.e: The square around the cathedral is called Stephansplatz. Many shopping streets start there.
50513.m: St Stephen's Cathedral stands on Stephansplatz.

50514.q: What are the underground passages with graves beneath St Stephen's Cathedral called?
50514.e: There are catacombs under the cathedral. The graves of many people from earlier times lie there.
50514.m: There are catacombs under St Stephen's Cathedral.

50515.q: Which famous composer was born in Salzburg?
50515.e: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756. You can visit the house where he was born today.

50516.q: What is the big castle high above the city of Salzburg called?
50516.e: Hohensalzburg Fortress sits on a hill above the old town. It is one of the largest castles in Europe.

50517.e: The Salzach divides Salzburg into two parts. Many bridges cross the river.

50518.q: Which substance is the city of Salzburg named after?
50518.e: A lot of salt used to be mined near Salzburg. The salt made the city rich.

50519.q: What are the three peaks of Salzburger Nockerl meant to look like?
50519.e: Salzburger Nockerl is a fluffy sweet dish made from eggs. The three peaks are meant to remind you of the snowy mountains around Salzburg.
50519.m: Salzburger Nockerl look like snowy mountains.

50520.q: What takes place in Salzburg every summer?
a: A festival of music and theatre
A cycle race round the world
50520.e: The Salzburg Festival has existed for more than 100 years. Every summer, guests come from all over the world.
50520.m: Salzburg has its festival every summer.

50521.q: Which famous musical film about a singing family is set in Salzburg?
50521.e: The film tells the story of the Trapp family, who lived in Salzburg and sang together.
50521.m: The film The Sound of Music is set in Salzburg.

50522.q: Since 1996 the old town of Salzburg has been something special. What is it?
50522.e: The beautiful old town with its churches and squares has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996.
50522.m: The old town of Salzburg is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

50523.q: What is the capital of the Austrian state of Tyrol?
50523.e: Innsbruck is the capital of Tyrol. The city lies in a valley between high mountains.
50523.m: Innsbruck is the capital of Tyrol.

50524.q: Which country does the state of Tyrol belong to?
50524.e: Tyrol is one of the nine states of Austria. It also borders Switzerland.
50524.m: The state of Tyrol belongs to Austria.

50525.q: Which country does Tyrol border in the south?
50525.e: Italy lies south of Tyrol. The part there is called South Tyrol.
50525.m: Tyrol borders Italy in the south.
